articles.title: Tom Brady's NFL Power Rankings: Caleb Williams MVP Watch Has Begun; Chiefs Are Back
articles.summary: Tom Brady is ready to make big statements about the Chiefs and Bears, but he has another team at No. 1 in his first power rankings of the season.
articles.body: Tom Brady's power rankings are back for a third season, and before he reveals his first top-10 of the new season, there are a few rules the GOAT has. One, in order to make this week's top 10, you've had to have won in Week 1. Two, the power rankings are all about what you've done lately, not what you can be. And three, if you have any complaints, direct them to the new FOX Sports digital show "Gronk & Jules." So, now that's out of the way, let's dive into Brady's first top 10 of the 2026 NFL season. #10 BengalsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: They had a great win against a very good Bucs team. I thought that Bucs team was going to go into Cincy and upset some people. Sorry to Ja’Marr Chase and all those fantasy owners. Trust me, you’ve got nothing to worry about. #9 LionsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: If you turned this one off early, you’re probably wondering why the Lions aren’t higher. But you really don’t want to see how this one went down. I think it’s very brave of these teams to go for 2 [to win the game like the Saints did]. It’s basically a 45/50% chance of making it. That’s what the stats say. Sometimes, I think you should make the other team beat you. But when you’re the road team against a good team, sometimes I don’t mind going for broke. #8 JaguarsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: How about the Jags? At No. 8, they ran it up against Cleveland. That’s what a lot of people forgot about Jacksonville last season. They won 13 games last year. Keep an eye out for this team. Liam Coen, really impressed, man. Keep it up. #7 ChiefsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: Kenneth Walker, he’s your [Super Bowl LX] MVP and the Chiefs are sitting at No. 7. Patrick Mahomes, are you kidding me? He might be able to contribute something to this offense as well. He wasn’t avoiding any contact [on Monday night]; I’m sure of that. I think, in a lot of ways, he’s back to [being] Patrick Mahomes. What do I mean by that? His leadership, discipline, tenacity — all of those things were on display. He’s going to pick up some steam. He’s missed some football, missed a lot of the offseason. But never sleep on No. 15 for the Chiefs. Why are we counting them out? Never count them out. I always felt like when you’ve got a great coach and you’ve got a great QB, and that organization has championship standards … watch out, man. #6 EaglesNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: KB and I, we were on the call in Philly, and the Eagles are knocking on the door of the top five. They knocked a little rust off, but they took care of business, starting 1-0 in the division. They know how to start fast. I like this team. They’re always going to play great defense. Once they figure out how to run the ball a little bit better, and they’ve still got Saquon [Barkley] back there and Tank Bigsby — they’re making those explosive plays. That’s the formula that set them up a few years ago, too. #5 BillsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: In our top five, you can shuffle a lot of teams here, but remember, when in doubt, my rankings are always the correct ones. The Bills are starting at five. That was a huge win in Houston. Houston had one of the best defenses in the league last year, and there’s going to be arguments to put Buffalo at the top of the list. But they were a dropped pick away from being off the [list] entirely. We know Josh [Allen], we know James Cook — they’re going to move the ball all year long. But those Bills fans are waiting for January at this point. Who can blame them? #4 RavensNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: Another team with a new head coach, Jesse Minter. Lamar [Jackson] dominated in Indy. They brought in Minter for this defense, but I’ll be watching [offensive coordinator] Declan Doyle and what he does with the weapons on this offense. It looked pretty good the other night. They’ll need the depth chart to step up at receiver for a few weeks. But Baltimore fans, guess what? You should be excited. #3 49ersNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: We now have the definitive guide on how to travel to Australia now, right? I think people talked more about that than the game this past week. Hats off to the Niners and Kyle Shanahan for tuning out a lot of the B.S., a lot of the noise and doing what they do: dominate a great Rams team Down Under. Brock [Purdy], quick word of advice: Keep throwing it to Mike Evans. He’s really good at catching the football, especially when you get close to the end zone. #2 BearsNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: The Caleb Williams MVP watch is under way. They put 59 on Carolina in Week 1. Ben Johnson wants the highest-scoring offense ever. But how about a little defense from this team when they get back to Chicago? Or, you know what, screw it — keep scoring 59 points. I’m an offensive guy, either way works. They make it look easy — 300 yards rushing, Caleb does his thing and when guys aren’t open, he scrambles. When they get that offense rolling, it’s hard to stop. I saw it a lot last year. I know we’re going to see it a lot this year. #1 SeahawksNew ranking1-0 Brady's thoughts: I don’t care, to be the champ, you’ve gotta beat the champ. When you win the Super Bowl and the Super Bowl rematch in the first game back, I don’t care who is playing QB, you’ve got to get the top spot. The defense, they haven’t skipped a beat. And I’ve got another secret QB hack for Drew Lock: As long as Sam [Darnold’s] out, throw it anywhere on JSN’s (Jaxon Smith-Njigba) side of the field; he’s going to come down with it.

articles.title: Bleacher Report's Expert Week 2 2026 NFL Picks and Predictions
articles.summary: In the first few weeks of the NFL season, we're all feeling out these teams, and even some head coaches are figuring out their clubs after resting starters in the preseason.
articles.body:
In the first few weeks of the NFL season, we're all feeling out these teams, and even some head coaches are figuring out their clubs after resting starters in the preseason.

Regardless, Bleacher Report's expert crew can find the edge on the point spreads to make early profit. Analysts Gary Davenport , Brad Gagnon , Kris Knox , Moe Moton , and Brent Sobleski , along with editors Wes O'Donnell and Ian Hanford , made it out of Week 1 with a winning record on lone-wolf picks. There are two more this week.

As you can see in the Week 1 standings below, Moton leads the group, and our panel was mostly .500 or better.

Let's dive into Week 2, starting with a big-time matchup between the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills Thursday night. Our crew is nearly split on that game, and two analysts have strong opinions for their side.

Lines are from FanDuel as of Wednesday, Sept. 16, at 4 p.m. ET. Check FanDuel for the latest odds info. Information on public betting trends is courtesy of the Action Network . ATS records are provided by Team Rankings .

Detroit Lions (1-0) at Buffalo Bills (1-0)

I don't trust either defense to let either offense pull away here. This strikes me as a game that will come down to a last-minute or overtime field goal.

In Week 1, the Detroit Lions' passing attack struggled early. Based on Next Gen Stats via NFL.com's Kevin Patra , Jared Goff's disparity in pass efficiency between snaps under center (9-of-17 for 72 yards) and in shotgun formation (17-of-22 for 134 yards and two touchdowns) is worth noting going forward.

On a separate note, coming off a four-touchdown performance against the Houston Texans' vaunted defense, Josh Allen gets a matchup with the Lions secondary without its starting safeties, All-Pro Kerby Joseph and Pro Bowler Brian Branch. He should feast on Detroit's pass defense as the Bills get their first win at the new Highmark Stadium by a touchdown.

Carolina Panthers (0-1) at Atlanta Falcons (0-1)

Lost in the Carolina Panthers' Week 1 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears, they played well offensively. Head coach Dave Canales' decision to hand off play-calling duties to offensive coordinator Brad Idzik could help Bryce Young's development.

Young threw for 361 yards, three touchdowns and an interception in defeat. If he posts half that stat line against the Atlanta Falcons, Carolina can win the game. With Michael Penix Jr. still recovering from knee surgery, the Falcons will start a banged-up Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) or journeyman backup Cooper Rush at quarterback.

If the Panthers sell out to stop Bijan Robinson after giving up 291 rushing yards last week, they should be able to win this toss-up matchup. The Falcons aren't nearly as prolific offensively as the Bears.

It's probably safe to say the Panthers won't give up 59 points again this week, regardless of who is playing QB for the Falcons. It's hard to take too much away from the teams' opening games outside of saying "the Panthers' defense is gorydamn terrible" — "the Bears' offense looks really dangerous" — and/or "the Falcons were actually in that Week 1 game at Pittsburgh with Cooper Rush at QB... until that pick-six" — albeit against a Steelers team that played exactly how you'd expect the Steelers to play.

So something's gotta give in this divisional matchup, and I'll take the points home because I don't believe in either team right now.

Panthers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

New Orleans Saints (0-1) at Baltimore Ravens (1-0)

This line is disrespectful to the New Orleans Saints, who erased a 21-point road deficit in Detroit and almost pulled off an outright upset in overtime. The Saints took some time to get going in the Motor City, but they have enough offensive firepower to keep the score margin within one possession.

The Saints' aerial attack will pose a legitimate threat. Tyler Shough can sling it; he threw for 410 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in Week 1. Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson racked up 20 receptions for a combined 305 yards and two touchdowns.

The Baltimore Ravens could be down two receivers. Ja'Kobi Lane will undergo wrist surgery, per CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . Zay Flowers sat out the second half of the previous week because of a hamstring injury. As of Wednesday, he's questionable at best. After an 18-point win over the Indianapolis Colts, Baltimore has to edge out the Saints in a more competitive one-possession game.

The second-half surge the Saints provided in Week 1 does make this spread worrisome. Tyler Shough and Co. are going to be difficult to deal with all season. However, the Baltimore Ravens were among the most impressive teams to open the season, particularly on offense where new coordinator Declan Doyle seemingly found the right recipe to unlock Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry and the talented group. Even with injuries at wide receiver, the Ravens should be able to execute at a high level and keep rolling.

Saints: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

Green Bay Packers (0-1) at New York Jets (1-0)

The Packers admittedly looked, um, yeah in blowing a big lead to a backup quarterback in Minnesota. The Jets, on the other hand, like won a game—on purpose and everything. But this spread isn't as big as the gap between the two teams. Order is restored to the universe Sunday at MetLife.

By no means do I trust the Jets, but I'll take that hook for a team feeling good in its home opener against an opponent that didn't look close to right in Week 1. Green Bay is hurting right now. The Jets will eventually hit a wall but I'm not convinced that happens here.

Packers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Minnesota Vikings (1-0) at Chicago Bears (1-0)

The Bears dropped 59 points on the Panthers last week. The Vikings will probably be starting Carson Wentz under center. So why take the points? Two reasons. The first is that Minnesota's defense is a fair bit better than Carolina's. The second is that Chicago's defense was turrible in Week 1. Not terrible. Turrible.

In Week 1, the Bears reminded me a lot of the 2024 Bengals. They feel like a team that can score almost at will, but one that may need to score at a high clip to win games. I don't trust Chicago's defense at this point in the season, but what I trust even less is Carson Wentz in a back-and-forth battle with Caleb Williams.

Bears: Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) at Houston Texans (0-1)

The Texans defense got lit up by Josh Allen and the Bills in Week 1, but I think the more important takeaway is C.J. Stroud looking sharp to go along with a strong run game. The Bengals scored 33 points against Tampa Bay in Week 1, but I think that was more about their defense forcing four turnovers than a prolific offense. I like the Texans' pass-rush to make Joe Burrow uncomfortable while the secondary locks up Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins as Houston gets a bounce-back win.

The Texans defense surrendering over 400 yards ranked among the most surprising outcomes in Week 1. Obviously, Bills quarterback Josh Allen had a lot to say in that matter. Still, Joe Burrow is no slouch, and the Cincinnati Bengals are far more talented at wide receiver.

Even if Houston does a better job slowing Cincinnati's offense, the Bengals' defense came to play this season by creating four turnovers and four sacks in the opener. This contest is an early litmus test to find out whether the Bengals can propel themselves into the AFC's elite, and they should do so.

Pittsburgh Steelers (1-0) at New England Patriots (0-1)

The Steelers offense remained a mostly dismal watch in Mike McCarthy's first game at the helm, but this is about the defense for me. The Patriots' offensive line still has issues, and the offense just lost its top playmaker in A.J. Brown for an extended period of time. New England is getting the favorable nod as the home team here, but I think T.J. Watt and the Pittsburgh defense make life difficult for Maye and make this game ugly enough that it stays within a field goal in the end.

Nothing has really changed for the Steelers despite Mike McCarthy replacing Mike Tomlin after 19 seasons. That's both good and bad. We know who the Steelers are right now. The Patriots, meanwhile, imploded in the opening-night Super Bowl rematch. More specifically, Drake Maye imploded.

The Pats' Bowl run a year ago was aided by a well-documented cupcake schedule, sure, but they still had to play and win the football games. This is a risk, but I'm backing the home favorites to rebound against a Steelers team that was 3-5 ATS in road games a year ago.

Steelers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Moton, Sobleski

Cleveland Browns (0-1) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-1)

Baker Mayfield has only faced the Browns once in his career, losing as QB of the Panthers in 2022. I'm not expecting the same result this time. The Browns were listless in every way against the Jaguars in Week 1. Trevor Lawrence shredded the defense, and the Cleveland offense struggled to find any rhythm. I think Mayfield and the Tampa Bay offense bounce back from a turnover-prone Week 1 and coast to an easy win here.

It's revenge SZN for Baker Mayfield. Not only does the Buccaneers quarterback need to redeem himself after a three-turnover performance in Week 1, he now gets to face the team that jettisoned him aside for the struggling quarterback the Cleveland Browns plan to start.

Mayfield is going to do everything in his power to bury his old team and prove it made the wrong decision—even if everyone already knows the franchise did. An exclamation point is necessary considering the bad blood between these two parties.

Buccaneers: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Philadelphia Eagles (1-0) at Tennessee Titans (0-1)

To be fair, while the Eagles won in Week 1, they didn't look especially good doing it—on either side of the ball. But while Philly was grinding out a win, the Titans were getting dusted. At home. By the New York Jets. Saquon goes nuts. Cam Ward flees for his life for four quarters. Fly Eagles Fly and whatnot.

It doesn't look like any of us are backing the Titans, and I can understand why. In Week 1, Tennessee looked like a team that could be picking at the top of the draft again this year.

That said, I could see a path to a Titans cover here. Philly's defense looked average at best against the run on Sunday, and its offense looked a lot like the uneven unit we saw in 2025. If first-time coordinator Sean Mannion doesn't find an early groove calling plays, I could see Tennessee keeping it close at home.

Eagles: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Jacksonville Jaguars (1-0) at Denver Broncos (0-1)

They say you shouldn't overreact to what happens in Week 1, but the difference in the level of execution between the Jaguars and Broncos in their respective openers was jarring. The Broncos were sloppy as can be on both sides of the ball, while the last time Jacksonville lost in the regular season was November 9. The Jaguars win outright—and what we thought we knew about the AFC gets snowglobed.

This is a tough one, but I'm riding with the home team. Bo Nix is 14-3 in his regular-season career at Mile High, and I'm expecting a motivated team after a disappointing Week 1 loss to the Chiefs. The Jaguars defense was dominant in its opener, but Denver isn't Cleveland, and I expect the Broncos to bring them back down to Earth. This will be a close one, but Denver hangs on by a field goal.

Jaguars: Davenport, Knox, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Las Vegas Raiders (1-0) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-1)

I'm not about to back the Chargers and hand away a touchdown considering what we saw from that team in Week 1. Could they bounce back? Absolutely, but this Raiders team looked very prepared for Week 1 under Klink Kubiak. Las Vegas has a lot more talent than people realize, and very little to lose. I think the Silver and Black keep this close. Laying a full touchdown with a Jim Harbaugh offense that posted 14 points and held the ball for under 23 minutes in Week 1 is asking for trouble.

It's easy to rationalize a Raiders cover here. In Week 1, they beat the Miami Dolphins by 14, and the Los Angeles Chargers looked dreadful in a 26-14 loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

However, Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins threw two interceptions along with three touchdowns, and if All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers (meniscus trim) isn't back for this game, he won't have a reliable downfield threat to minimize those mistakes.

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh believes resting his starters during the preseason hurt his team in the season opener. Even if wideout Ladd McConkey sits out with a rib injury, Los Angeles should be more prepared to play regular-season football against an offensively limited Raiders squad.

Also, under Harbaugh, the Chargers have cleared this point spread in all four matchups against the Raiders, winning by an average of 13 points .

Chargers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Seattle Seahawks (1-0) at Arizona Cardinals (1-0)

This is an indictment on Drew Lock, who will now match up with a team that is feeling good and will have actually fully prepared for him to start in place of the injured Sam Darnold. That's a lot of points for a divisional matchup with a backup quarterback involved, especially considering that these teams split the season series in 2025. The Cards are not void of offensive talent, and it's entirely possible new head coach Mike LaFleur has tapped into something.

Do the Cardinals have something special going on in Mike LaFleur's first season as head coach or were the Chargers just not ready to play football last week? I'm going to lean on the latter. Seattle has had over a week to prep for life without Sam Darnold at QB, and the defending champions laying less than a touchdown in Arizona against a Cardinals team that was 1-7 ATS at home last season is too enticing to pass up.

Seahawks: Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

Miami Dolphins (0-1) at San Francisco 49ers (1-0)

The 49ers haven't won a home game by two touchdowns since December 2024. Now they're arriving back from a trip across the world. They're lucky to be playing a weak opponent, and I do think they'll get out to a nice lead. That said, this has backdoor cover written all over it.

This is a lot of points to cover, even for a team that looked like the class of the NFC in Week 1. However, I just can't envision Miami putting up many points against a healthy 49ers defense. If the 49ers don't run away with this one, it'll be due to jet lag, not the Dolphins.

49ers: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell, Sobleski

Washington Commanders (0-1) at Dallas Cowboys (0-1)

The Dallas Cowboys offense is more potent at home than on the road. Last year, they averaged 29.9 points at AT&T Stadium compared to 25.8 points elsewhere, per Team Rankings .

With the same offensive core, the Cowboys will be much sharper offensively against the Washington Commanders than they were at MetLife Stadium in a Week 1 28-20 loss to the New York Giants.

Keep in mind that Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels had a rough season-opening outing in first-year play-caller David Blough's offense. Washington didn't engineer a touchdown drive until the fourth quarter of that game. Cowboys win this one by at least a touchdown.

The Cowboys had it coming in Week 1, at least in a historical aspect. Their dominance over the New York Giants for the past five, 10 and 20 years was well-documented, and that wasn't the same Giants team they were accustomed to roping like cattle. Now the Commanders come to town, a team that got shafted with two straight divisional road games to open the season.

The bad news for Dallas is the things the Commanders do well, like keeping drives alive and eating clock, not turning the ball over and just being annoying enough to frustrate opposing fan bases, is basically what the Cowboys just experienced against the Giants in Week 1. The Cowboys will probably win this game, but they were 1-3 as home favorites ATS a year ago, and I'm not passing up a field goal with a hook in this scenario.

Cowboys: Davenport, Hanford, Knox, Moton, Sobleski

Indianapolis Colts (0-1) at Kansas City Chiefs (1-0)

The Chiefs looked like they had something to prove in their dominant MNF win over the Broncos, and I don't see much changing this week. The Colts offense doesn't present a major threat outside of Jonathan Taylor. The defense was gashed by Derrick Henry on the ground in Week 1, and now it faces Kenneth Walker III, who looked like the ideal fit in Andy Reid's offense against Denver. I think the Chiefs make another statement here with a double-digit win.

The Colts were easily one of the biggest disappointments to open the 2026 campaign. Conversely, the Chiefs were among the most impressive. The selection of Indianapolis for this particular matchup comes across as counterintuitive.

At the same time, this setup screams of desperation. Yes, it's only Week 2, but the Colts were embarrassed during their home opener. Plus, this coaching staff knows if things don't turn around quickly, it may not make it through the season. The Chiefs are going to get everything the Colts have during Sunday Night Football .

Chiefs: Davenport, Gagnon, Hanford, Knox, Moton, O'Donnell

New York Giants (1-0) at Los Angeles Rams (0-1)

The Giants and Rams are both coming off of emotional divisional battles in prime time. I think that will benefit the home team in this matchup, even if Los Angeles doesn't have much of a home-field advantage.

I think we may see some overconfidence from New York following Sunday night's big win over the rival Cowboys. I think we'll see some anger from the Rams after their blunder down under put them at the bottom of the NFC West. With extra time to prepare, I think Sean McVay will push his team to a statement win to cap Week 2.

The Rams could absolutely explode in this game. Sean McVay's team scored only seven points in Australia, lost Myles Garrett for a while, and probably wish they simply missed their flight in the first place. They return home on MNF with a lot to prove. They're better than the Giants across the board, and most dangerously, in the passing game against a New York secondary that is still starting Deonte Banks.

But this is a prove-it game for New York, too. Can it retain any momentum after the most complete victory the franchise has experienced since, probably, the 2011 season? This is a risk, but I'll roll the dice with Big Blue at least covering and proving it'll be a tough out all season.

Giants: Davenport, Hanford, O'Donnell, Sobleski

articles.title: “How insensitive. How immature”: ESPN’s Shae Cornette tells Peyton and Eli Manning’s nephew Arch Manning to know better after Texas QB laughed at AI video depicting violence against Holly Rowe
articles.summary: NFL News: A viral AI-generated video was circulating online about ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe.The video showed Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian .
articles.body: A viral AI-generated video was circulating online about ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe.The video showed Texas Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping Rowe during a sideline interview.At the team’s weekly media availability, Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning spoke about that viral video.Peyton and Eli Manning’s nephew said, “I’ve seen a few AI edits of stuff. But that’s about it.I saw an AI edit of Sark [Steve Sarkisian]’s interview [reporters laugh in the background]...You all seen that one? That’s a good one! [Arch starts laughing uncontrollably]...Of him slapping Holly Rowe? [Arch laughing continues]...Yeah, it’s hilarious!”Arch Manning apologizes for laughing at Holly Rowe and Steve Sarkisian’s viral AI videoAs soon as Arch Manning made that comment about ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe, his press meet video went viral.Everyone started sharing their own opinion. Criticism of his comments came forward. And so did his heartfelt apology via Instagram story.Arch Manning’s apology:“In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it. It’s easy to say I didn’t mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people.I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that. I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she personally had to deal with because of my comments.I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward.”Holly Rowe accepts Arch Manning’s apologyArch’s apology reached AI-video victim Holly Rowe. Rowe responded through her Instagram story, tagging Arch’s apology:“Thank you, Arch. I appreciate our conversation about this - which will remain private. Apology accepted. We move forward with respect and kindness for one another.”The Arch Manning episode was not going to end there. Arch said something insensitive about a viral violence-against-Rowe-promoting video. Arch apologized for it. And then Rowe accepted Arch’s apology.The episode was not going to end there. It was going to attract some backlash from Rowe’s colleagues. And that’s exactly what ESPN’s First Take host Shae Cornette did.Shae Cornette teaches Arch Manning a valuable lessonShae Cornette sat alongside longtime ESPN’s First Take host Stephen A. Smith and said,“Okay, so Stephen A. and I learned about this yesterday, and so I’ll give my quick take on this,” Cornette said.“And when I first heard Arch’s comments and watched that press conference, my initial reaction was, my goodness, how insensitive, how immature, and kind of, quite frankly, like how dare he say that, especially about Holly and the way he was laughing about it.As the day progressed, I thought to myself, okay, when you have this last name, and you play at this university, and you wear that on your sleeve every day, you have to know better.”Cornette continued, “And maybe that’s unfair, given his age and his immaturity level still and what he’s going through at his age. But that is just the reality of the situation that comes with it.He’s apologized. He had a conversation with Holly Roe, which I love. Now, I do wish his apology was vocal, was on video as opposed to in text. But nonetheless, now we move forward.”“But what I do hope is, obviously, this was a very strong learning lesson for him. You don’t necessarily need to be laughing about a video that provokes violence, especially towards women. And so Arch hopefully will do better,” added Cornette.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: It’s one of the most interesting weeks of the NFL season. Here’s what you need to know for Week 2
articles.summary: Week 2 is one of the most fascinating weeks of the entire NFL season. This is the week when fans find out if they completely overreacted to what happened in Week 1 – or if that reaction was actually justified.
articles.body: Week 2 is one of the most fascinating weeks of the entire NFL season. This is when fans find out if they completely overreacted to what happened in Week 1 – or if that reaction was actually justified. So, what was real and what was just a one-week mirage? Here are five things to know about this week’s slate of games. Bills open new Highmark Stadium After 53 seasons at their old home in Orchard Park, the Bills are moving into a brand-new Highmark Stadium on Thursday night when they host the Detroit Lions. The new stadium sits right next to the old one, cost just over $2.1 billion and, yes, there is still no roof. So the Bills should still have that cold-weather, home-field advantage when teams come north in December and January. The open-air stadium has a capacity of 60,108. The stadium hasn’t received rave reviews from everyone, with some fans complaining about obstructed-view seats. It’s also considerably smaller than the old Highmark Stadium, with the Bills saying the reduced capacity is designed to create a better overall fan experience. And if you want to be there for the first regular-season game, it won’t be cheap. The get-in price for Thursday night’s opener was going for more than $400 as of Wednesday. Buffalo is riding high after a thrilling Week 1 win over the Houston Texans, while the Lions squeaked by the New Orleans Saints by one point. Expect plenty of points when these two meet on Thursday Night Football. Bears offense: The best ever? Before the season, Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson said he wanted his offense to score more points than any team in NFL history. Well … so far, so good. The Bears found the end zone eight times in a historic season opener, beating the Carolina Panthers 59-37. Chicago tied a franchise record with six rushing touchdowns and scored the most points in a season opener in franchise history. If you’re wondering, Peyton Manning and the 2013 Denver Broncos hold the NFL record for most points in a season with 606, so only 547 to go for the Bears. And Chicago gets an extra game compared to those Broncos. Caleb Williams was awesome through the air and on the ground, combining for four touchdowns. He completed 21 of 29 passes for 269 yards and threw two touchdowns, while rushing for another 65 yards and two more scores. The Bears have never had a 4,000-yard passer in franchise history, but it certainly looks like Williams has a chance to finally end that drought this season. Next up: Chicago hosts the Minnesota Vikings in its home opener Sunday. Burrow vs. the Texans’ defense One of the most disappointing units in Week 1 was the Houston Texans defense. There was a lot of chatter this offseason talking about how good this defense was going to be. Then, in the opener — at home — Josh Allen and the Bills hung 36 points on them. Even worse, when the Texans had opportunities to make plays and win late, they couldn’t. Houston dropped an interception and then gave up a 34-yard touchdown. And now the Texans defense goes from Josh Allen to a Joe Burrow led Cincinnati Bengals squad. Burrow didn’t have the sharpest opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, throwing for 254 yards, one touchdown and one interception. But if the Texans defense plays like it did against Buffalo, it could be another long afternoon in Houston. The Texans started 0-3 last season before rallying to make the playoffs. That’s a hole they definitely don’t want to find themselves in again. NFC South… woof The only division in football that failed to win a game in Week 1? The NFC South. The Buccaneers, Atlanta Falcons, New Orleans Saints and Carolina Panthers all lost. But give Saints coach Kellen Moore some credit for going for two and the win instead of playing for a tie against the Lions. No one likes ties. The good news for the NFC South is the division is likely getting one win this week because the Falcons host the Panthers. Baker Mayfield and the Bucs should also have a good chance to get into the win column as big home favorites against the Cleveland Browns. The Bucs just need Mayfield to not lose three fumbles. The Saints, meanwhile, get another tough road game to open the season as they head to Baltimore to face the Ravens. Giants and Jets! New York football fans, enjoy this one. For the first time since 2009, the Giants and Jets both started the season with a win. When was the last time they both started 2-0, you ask? Also 2009. In fact, both teams started 3-0 that season. Right now, 3-0 probably sounds like a dream for both franchises. The Giants head to Los Angeles in Week 2 to face an angry – and now well-rested – Rams team. Sean McVay’s squad will have had 10 days between its game in Australia and Monday night’s matchup against the Giants. Is that enough time to recover from the jet lag they were trying to avoid in the first place before getting stomped by the San Francisco 49ers? The Rams will be without Myles Garrett for a month or more following knee surgery, but we could see the return of three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald after a two-plus-year retirement. John Harbaugh and the Giants had a great game plan in Week 1, with Jaxson Dart and Cam Skattebo running wild against the Dallas Cowboys. Can those two keep it going – and, just as importantly, stay healthy? That’s one of the biggest questions surrounding the Giants this season. The Jets, meanwhile, host the Green Bay Packers on Sunday. We still don’t really know what to make of the Jets because they beat Tennessee in Week 1 – and the Titans might once again be one of the worst teams in football. Green Bay comes into the matchup trying to rebound from a historic collapse against Minnesota. The Packers led 22-10 with less than 20 minutes remaining before getting outscored 29-0 the rest of the way in a 39-22 loss. Minnesota became the first team in NFL history to trail by at least 12 points with less than 20 minutes remaining and still win by at least 17. articles.title: "I don't give a f***": Aaron Rodgers has had enough of Steelers offense criticism after week 1 leaves Pittsburgh facing serious questions
articles.summary: NFL News: Pittsburgh beat Atlanta 20-13 in Week 1, but the win came with an asterisk. The Steelers' offense ranked second-to-last in NFL Offense Impact Ratings .
articles.body: Pittsburgh beat Atlanta 20-13 in Week 1, but the win came with an asterisk. The Steelers' offense ranked second-to-last in NFL Offense Impact Ratings and spent most of the afternoon stuck in neutral. The run game barely showed up. Drives died without warning. Jaylen Warren fumbled at the worst possible moment. Yet when reporters tried pinning Aaron Rodgers down on all of it, he made one thing crystal clear: he is not interested in the noise.Why is Aaron Rodgers dismissing concerns about the Steelers' offensive balance?The criticism coming Pittsburgh's way after Week 1 is not hard to understand. Rodgers threw the ball 40 times, finishing 24-of-40 for 221 yards and a touchdown. That would be fine on its own, but the ground game behind him collapsed entirely. Warren gained just 46 yards on 10 carries. Rico Dowdle managed 15 yards on eight attempts. The offensive line generated almost no push, and Pittsburgh's team rushing average sat under three yards per carry by the end of the night.That kind of imbalance usually prompts a quarterback to acknowledge the problem publicly. Rodgers went the other way."The consistency and the balance stuff is all for, you know, talking head fodder," Rodgers said. "I'm not worried about the balance. Balance comes naturally."His reasoning is worth following because it is not entirely without logic. In his view, the blueprint is to score early, build a lead, and let the run game develop from there. Avoiding three-and-outs creates more opportunities to run the ball. "If you don't have five three-and-outs, you get more run opportunities too," he explained.The problem is that Pittsburgh's offense had those stalling stretches. A lot of them. So while the theory is sound, Week 1 did not produce the kind of execution that makes the argument easy to buy.What did Aaron Rodgers say about target distribution among his receivers?The target distribution question came up too, and Rodgers had even less patience for it. "I don't give a (expletive) about the target list," he said bluntly. "I don't care about any of that."Asked why, he kept it short. "Because the ball goes to the open guy," Rodgers said.He went a step further, drawing a clear line between what gets discussed inside the locker room and what gets discussed outside of it. "I don't wanna hear people talking about it. Nobody in the locker room talks about their targets. That's all for you guys to talk about," Rodgers said.He did acknowledge that certain players need the ball more based on matchup and scheme. Everyone else, in his words, just "gets in the flow." That part, at least, is how most offenses around the league operate.Still, Pittsburgh heads to New England this Sunday to face the defending AFC champion Patriots. A road game against a quality opponent does not leave much margin for another uneven offensive performance. The defense can only carry so much, and Rodgers knows that better than anyone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

The stadium cost approximately $2.2 billion and boasts a capacity of 60,108 for football games. It is replacing the old Highmark Stadium, more commonly known as Ralph Wilson Stadium, which served as the Bills' home for 53 years.

New Highmark Stadium hosted two preseason games, but Thursday night's matchup between the Bills and Detroit Lions will serve as its official opening contest.

In a game that should be high-scoring, expect the Lions to go to the air more often than they did in Week one, especially because they aren't likely to jump out to a big lead early on the Bills as they did against the Saints.

articles.summary: Thursday Screencaps heads to Buffalo for the historic Highmark Stadium opener as fans debate the OJ walk of fame and a mysterious baby bison cage.
articles.body: Welcome to Thursday Screencaps, but this isn't just another Thursday. This morning, I'm coming to you from suburban Buffalo where I'm holed up in a condo pumping out this edition before hopping in the car and heading down to Highmark Stadium for tonight's historic Bills home opener. Last night was all about getting our bearings straight, so we went to Big Tree Inn, the legendary Bills bar just down the street from Highmark where we bellied up to the bar to talk to some old salty dawgs who'd seen a few things over the years. One of those guys, Scott in Arizona, told me tales of his past adventures. He swears there was a time back in the late 90s or early 2000s when he watched a visiting quarterback take a woman upstairs at Big Tree Inn. As Scott tells the story, on his way back down, the visiting QB fell down the stairs and ended up on the following week's injury report. He told me the name, but I can't report such things. All I can say is that it was a BIG name. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Were the wings any good at Big Tree Inn? Not really, but I wasn't there for the wings. I was there to feel the energy. I was there to hear from these fans who've been in the trenches and have felt the heartache and have lived through snowy Sundays when it looked like this franchise might leave Buffalo. Tonight, that all changes with the introduction of the new spaceship stadium that rises from the earth, unlike Ralph Wilson that sat down in a bowl. Are Bills fans really ready for amenities? Aren't they going to miss the blue collar Ralph Wilson Stadium? When I asked Scott in Arizona that question, you could see the apprehension on his face. How could the Bills do OJ like that? I'm furious we missed this press conference, but I had no idea it was going on. I'm not even interested in forming an opinion one way or the other on if OJ should have a spot in the team's walk of fame, but you're damn right I want to have a camera on a lady making a strong case for OJ based on his on-field accomplishments. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Now, let's keep in mind that the area where this walk of fame is located is called the "Family Circle." I think we can all agree, even ignoring the whole double murder thing, is that OJ wasn't exactly the best family man. Maybe you honor his legacy with the team in a different place inside the stadium. What's up with this cage out front of Highmark Stadium? The locals believe the team is getting a baby bison mascot and the baby bison will be put into this cage before tonight's game. That's what they say. As your boots on the ground, we'll go take a look later today. Odds and ends from Buffalo: • Scott in Arizona said the airport was out of rental cars with 100 reservations going unfilled on Wednesday. • The hotel scene here is terrible. But...this Airbnb in Williamsville that we're staying in for $300 per night is amazing. Brand new. Walked in and the AC was set at 68. Great shower pressure. This sure beats roughing it at some Red Roof Inn off I-90. • The local brewery here in Williamsville was PACKED last night at 8 p.m. A buddy of mine stopped by for a drink last night and said it's because in about 6-7 weeks, the locals are buried in snow, so they have to enjoy the weather before it's too late. • The local news didn't cover a single piece of non-Bills news for 90 minutes this morning. articles.title: Colin Kaepernick: The NFL is 'largely unchanged'
articles.summary: Colin Kaepernick shares his perspective on the NFL.
articles.body:
Listen and subscribe to Power Players with Brian Sozzi on Apple Podcasts , Amazon Music , Spotify , YouTube , or wherever you find your favorite podcasts.

Years after peacefully protesting systemic racism by kneeling during the National Anthem in an NFL game, Colin Kaepernick says not much has changed with the powerful sports league that he believes put him on a blacklist.

"I think the NFL is largely unchanged," the former NFL QB-turned-activist Kaepernick said in a new episode of the Power Players With Brian Sozzi podcast (video above; listen in below).

Kaepernick added, "Unfortunately, the most recent one that we saw was the race norming where they're measuring Black players' cognitive ability at a lower level to be able to deny them medical benefits after their playing careers. We saw in relation to myself and other players being targeted for the protest. There is a long history of work that they've done there. It's actually some of the work that Eric Reed combated while he was a part of the players' union. So I think largely unchanged there. I think there's a lot of phenomenal work they could be doing. I just don't know, and don't think they have the will to do it."

The NFL didn't return Yahoo Finance's request for comment.

Kaepernick is out with his memoir, "The Perilous Fight," chronicling his childhood right through to the present day of being a father in the public spotlight.

Kaepernick was a standout quarterback at the University of Nevada before being drafted by the San Francisco 49ers in 2011. He quickly hit the national stage in 2012 when he took over as the 49ers' starting QB and led the franchise to an appearance in Super Bowl XLVII.

His career trajectory shifted dramatically in 2016 when he began kneeling during the national anthem to protest systemic racism and police brutality in the United States.

Following that season, he became a free agent and remained unsigned by any NFL team, leading him to file a grievance alleging league owners colluded to keep him out. The matter was later settled.

Since exiting the league, Kaepernick has transformed into a prominent civil rights activist and entrepreneur, founding organizations like the Know Your Rights Camp and educational tech platform Lumi Story AI.

Key to all his businesses: drive impact in the community. Kaepernick is especially focused on Lumi Story AI which is giving students the tools to navigate the push to AI derived learning.

"How do we help them develop and build the skills so we don't have 70% of students or approximately 35 million students falling behind there. And as we're doing that work, part of the reason the focus is there, we have a world that's being built at present and in the future with AI, which today is all natural language. And we aren't building the foundational skills to allow them to access the tools that they're going to need later in their life," he added.

articles.title: NFL Draft stock report: sell- Dante Moore, QB, Oregon Ducks
articles.summary: Oregon has been the most surprisingly disappointing team, with their starting quarterback, Dante Moore, the most unexpectedly underperforming player
articles.body:
Dante Moore can ball out, there is no doubt about that. However, we have not seen that, through the first two games this year. We still have 10 games left to go (plus the postseason), but through the first two, Moore is absolutely all over the place.

As we enter week three, the Oregon Ducks have been the most surprisingly disappointing team, with their starting quarterback, Moore, the most unexpectedly underperforming player.

The Detroit native is a very smart, heady, analytical player. He also really put in the work this offseason, to try and get better.

So what's going wrong? Well, you can start with the fact that he has, what they would call in poker, "a tell."

Yes, he's unintentionally tipping his pitches.

Dante Moore's stance was GIVING AWAY run or pass almost every time.More balanced stance = RUNOne foot forward = PASSJust watch this. This is only from the first couple drives. And it kept happening ALL GAME. pic.twitter.com/DeIts4nNdZ — Oregon Updates (@oregon__updates) September 14, 2026

Dante Moore's stance was GIVING AWAY run or pass almost every time.More balanced stance = RUNOne foot forward = PASSJust watch this. This is only from the first couple drives. And it kept happening ALL GAME. pic.twitter.com/DeIts4nNdZ

Oregon Updates (@oregon__updates) September 14, 2026

It is astounding how Oregon, a program with as much money as any in college football (and thus, a very large staff of highly compensated coaches, staffer and other personnel), didn't see this coming.

Head coach Dan Lanning and his subordinates didn't notice this in practice? Well, maybe this is an easy fix, and then Moore will be back to his former self.

Because right now, there are major Jake Locker vibes- a college QB that could have declared for the draft when his stock was high, but came back to school for another year, and then saw his draft stock plummet.

It's a cautionary tale, to say the least.

It is often said that there is holding on nearly every play in the NFL, and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce admitted this week that he got away with it on Monday night.

Speaking Wednesday on his New Heights podcast (h/t Pro Football Talk's Michael David Smith ), Kelce acknowledged that he was fortunate to not be called for holding on quarterback Patrick Mahomes' 15-yard rushing touchdown during KC's 31-10 home win over the Denver Broncos in Week 1:

Can't do it. Almost cost us. That would've been Patrick Mahomes' second rushing touchdown called back in two plays, it was the same thing. That would've taken us out of the red zone. That was risky business. You know what? Sometimes you're just living right."

As seen in the video of Mahomes' touchdown run, Kelce did appear to get away with a hold on Broncos safety Talanoa Hufanga, as he essentially grabbed Hufanga's collar.

Mahomes had just gotten a touchdown run called back for holding on the previous play, as offensive tackles Kahlil Benson and Jaylon Moore were both whistled for the infraction.

The superstar quarterback's touchdown run on the ensuing play was significant since Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL suffered last season and showed that he is at least close to full health.

Regardless of the holding call that wasn't, the Chiefs were clearly the better team on Monday night, out-gaining the Broncos 392-176.

articles.title: NFL Thursday Night Football preview: Bills open their new stadium with a great matchup vs. Lions
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Bills are coming off an impressive win at Houston.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have been around since 1960 and they have played in only two home stadiums.

War Memorial Stadium was their home through the 1972 season, but the team quickly outgrew it. Then came Rich Stadium, which would undergo a few name changes that included Ralph Wilson Stadium and Highmark Stadium. There were 429 games and many great memories there. But eventually the Bills had to upgrade from that stadium too.

The Bills had one of the more outdated stadiums in the NFL. That's not the case anymore. New Highmark Stadium cost $2.2 billion and has its first regular-season game Thursday night against the Detroit Lions . While there have been complaints about obstructed views at some of the seats, overall the stadium looked luxurious during the preseason.

And Bills fans have a pretty good team residing in the new stadium.

The Bills are coming off a thrilling 36-31 win in Week 1 over the Houston Texans in which quarterback Josh Allen played a remarkable game, including a game-winning touchdown in the final two minutes. Allen is an MVP favorite and the Bills are a Super Bowl contender . Add the excitement over the new stadium, and it's a good time to be a Bills fan.

The regular-season opener in new Highmark Stadium should be a lot of fun. The Lions are a good and exciting team as well. While their Week 1 overtime win over the New Orleans Saints was closer than they'd hoped, especially after taking a 21-0 lead, they escaped with a win and have high hopes for the season. It's a team that won 15 games two seasons ago and still has most of the stars from that squad. There are some questions about an injured Lions secondary, which might just mean we see a lot of touchdowns.

One way or another, it will be a memorable night for the Bills franchise.

We could break it down in football terms here, but only one team has history at stake. You don't want to follow the pomp and circumstance of opening a new stadium with a loss. Nobody in Michigan will remember years from now if the Lions won a Week 2 game against an AFC team. But Bills fans will recall what happened in the first regular-season game at new Highmark Stadium (for the record, they won their first game at their previous stadium 9-7 over the New York Jets in 1973). There will be pressure on the Bills given the importance of the night in Western New York. Whatever happens will be part of the stadium's history.

Williams has established himself as a very good receiver but he's coming off a poor Week 1. Williams had multiple drops, though it didn't ultimately cost Detroit as the Lions went on to win 31-30 in overtime. Williams has had issues with drops throughout his career, but Detroit probably can't afford more if they want to beat the Bills. The Lions' offense is incredibly condensed: Jahmyr Gibbs , Amon-Ra St. Brown , Sam LaPorta and Williams accounted for 53 of 57 touches among skill position players in Week 1. They need all of those players at their best to beat a Bills team that is going to put up plenty of points. Williams can help keep Detroit in the game with a few big plays.

This line has been on the move. The lookahead was Bills -3, it reopened on Sunday night at -3.5 and it's now as high as Bills -5.5 at some sportsbooks. The total has also ticked up from 52.5 to 54.5, both because of how good each team's offense looked in Week 1 ... and how bad each team's defense played. With Josh Allen and Co. opening Highmark Stadium in Buffalo, it's going to be a tall task for the Lions to stay in this game if its secondary doesn't play better. The betting public is backing Buffalo to cover, and while I don't hate the pick, I'd target the Bills' team total instead. If Tyler Shough had 410 yards passing and led the Saints to 29 first downs (8-of-17 on third down), what will Allen do against Detroit's D?

Check out more of Ben's work at the Yahoo Sports betting hub .

Fantasy football storylines, by Scott Pianowski

The total is set in the 55 range for Bills and Lions tonight, so it's a juicy spot for fantasy managers. Here are three stories I'll have my eyes on.

1. Can this be D.J. Moore 's dream season? Although Moore was a target hog in Carolina and had one great year in Chicago , he's never gone past eight touchdowns in a season. Hopes are especially high for Moore in Buffalo after a 5-100-1 opener, and the Detroit secondary is ravaged by injury.

2. Will Jameson Williams bounce back? Williams left a bunch of points on the field last week, struggling with drops and focus. Given that he had nine targets and one running play called for him (botched by his hands), just 45 yards goes down as a disappointment. But the Lions have a narrow target tree, and Williams can score from anywhere on the field.

3. Can Dalton Kincaid keep the heavy usage? Kincaid was limited to 38% snaps last year, as the Bills helped him manage knee issues. He ran on 72% of the snaps in last week's opener, helping him produce a 5-130-0 line. Perhaps the timing is right for his breakout year.

articles.title: Week 2 NFL picks against the spread, predictions for every game: Cowboys try to rebound vs. Commanders
articles.summary: The Cowboys defense was terrible in the season opener.
articles.body:
If you didn't know it, you'd have never thought the Dallas Cowboys defense made a single change over the offseason.

Dallas looked as bad as ever on defense in the opener. The communication issues that plagued them last season hadn't gone away. They were pushed around by the New York Giants. The Cowboys got a new coordinator and five new starters (not counting linebacker DeMarvion Overshown returning from injury), and somehow nothing looked different. The Cowboys gave up the most points in franchise history last season. In Week 1, the Giants had the highest EPA ( expected points added ) per play in the entire NFL against Dallas' defense. Perhaps it was wrong to trust a rookie coordinator to be a magic cure and some good but not great players to completely fix the defense.

All offseason, the Cowboys were one of the most hyped teams. They spoke willingly about winning a Super Bowl even though they were 7-9-1 last season. Plenty of people who've grown tired of the attention the Cowboys get warned of falling for the same offseason buzz with Dallas. It's not like it has worked out for the past 30 years. And based on one game, maybe those critics were right.

The Cowboys come into Week 2 not talking about a Super Bowl anymore, but needing a win over the Washington Commanders and to avoid another embarrassing performance on defense. The defensive part shouldn't be too much to ask, but after last week it isn't a given.

Week 1 can provide some weird results. Some things we saw last week won't make any sense in a couple months. Maybe the Cowboys' performance, especially on defense, is one of those outliers. For this week we'll give the Cowboys another chance, against a Washington team that wasn't exactly smooth in its opener even though it nearly beat the Eagles. Cowboys -4 is the pick. And if Dallas plays as poorly as it did in New York, all of that offseason hype will look even sillier.

Here are the against the spread picks for the rest of the Week 2 games in the NFL:

Week 2 is interesting. We have to weigh what we saw in the opening week vs. what we know about these teams and thought of them over a long offseason. In Week 1, we saw Josh Allen look like Superman against a Texans defense that will be just fine, while the Lions had to successfully defend a two-point conversion to hang on to beat the Saints in overtime. The Bills are a good team, but so are the Lions. A letdown after going up 21-0 against New Orleans isn't ideal, but it happens. This will be a fun game, and a close one.

It's not comfortable to take the Buccaneers giving more than a touchdown. They might not be that good. But it's way harder to back the Browns as long as Deshaun Watson is their quarterback. And it's not like anything else looked good for Cleveland in Week 1.

You're going to hear about lookahead lines (point spreads posted before the previous week kicks off) a few times. In Week 2 it's an easy way to see overreactions to a one-game sample size. Last week the Packers were -5.5 for their game at the Jets (h/t to 4for4.com ). Now it's two points shorter. The Packers outgained the Vikings 419-239 and while the fourth quarter collapse was awful, it's not like they were outplayed. The Jets did outplay the Titans, but we might look back on that as the first sign that Tennessee is one of the NFL's worst teams. The Packers should still be the far better team here.

Tough to gauge this game because we don't know who is starting at quarterback for the Falcons. If it's Michael Penix Jr., clearly the Falcons have a better shot. If it's undrafted rookie Jack Strand, we could see another Max Brosmer story. Last year people went crazy about some preseason highlights of Brosmer with the Vikings, then the undrafted rookie played really poorly when he got a shot in the regular season. The Panthers haven't covered as a favorite since 2021 , which seems impossible. This is their week to do it.

I'd rather not take a road favorite this big early in the season. And there is going to be overreaction to Tennessee's Week 1 performance that I'd normally avoid. But it was troubling how bad the Titans were in the opener. Their offense was hideous. It's not going to be any easier against the Eagles' defense. Philadelphia had its own offensive issues in Week 1, but how do the Titans move the ball in this one?

I believe the Texans will have a top three defense this season. What we saw in Week 1 was Josh Allen announcing to the NFL world that he has reached a new level, which is scary. Houston's offense looked much improved in Week 1, which is a positive that could be something we're talking more about later on in the season. The Bengals won last week, but it's hard to live off turnovers and they needed all four they got to beat Tampa Bay. Cincinnati is still a slow-starting team and I won't overreact to the Texans losing to Allen's unbelievable outing in Week 1.

Oddsmakers really like Baltimore. They were high on the Ravens before the season started, and that looked smart as Baltimore steamrolled the Colts in Week 1. I have some concerns about the health of Baltimore's receivers, after Zay Flowers hurt his hamstring and Ja'Kobi Lane fractured his wrist. Lamar Jackson needs someone to throw to. Meanwhile, the Saints offense got off to a poor start but finished well enough to believe they can at least keep the Ravens honest.

Another tough pick without knowing exactly who is at quarterback for the Vikings. The guess is it's Carson Wentz after Kyler Murray's concussion. I have plenty of concerns about the Bears defense, but I know they'll score , even against Brian Flores' house of mirrors blitz concepts. I'd like to take the Vikings to fade some of the Bears hype, but can't depend on Wentz to outscore Chicago's offense.

The Steelers won and there still should be significant concerns about them. Their EPA on offense was 30th in the NFL and the success rate was 32nd, and that was at home against a mediocre Falcons defense. Their defensive numbers looked OK, but that was against Cooper Rush. I was not impressed with the Steelers. The Patriots lost and the week has been spent bashing Drake Maye, but an easier opponent, a home game and some extra rest will do New England well.

The lookahead line last week was Chargers -9.5. They looked awful losing to the Cardinals. But do we make much of the Raiders beating a Dolphins team that barely has an NFL roster? I don't buy that the Chargers are a terrible team all of a sudden. They just had a terrible game, which we've seen happen in Week 1 before. And the Chargers need to win with a brutal stretch of the schedule coming up.

A true test of not overreacting to Week 1. The Jaguars looked great. The Broncos couldn't have looked worse, with the offense flailing around and the defense forgetting how to tackle. This is a blind pick that the Broncos are much better than we saw last week and also their home-field advantage in September. The Broncos are 85-34-2 at home all-time in September. It's not easy to play at high altitude early in the season.

It's not going to be fun to back the Dolphins this season. The line of Raiders -3.5 last week was way, way too low. We haven't fully realized how bad Miami might be this season. Still, the 49ers could have a letdown after beating the Rams, and the fatigue from a long Australia trip could be real. It's just hard to trust the Dolphins to keep it close.

Seattle was -10 on the lookahead line. When Yahoo Sports' Ben Fawkes polled oddsmakers , they had the difference between Sam Darnold and Drew Lock at about 4.5 points. So the line has moved 1.5 points because the Cardinals played well against the Chargers? Seattle has a lot of extra rest, which helps not just to recover but to get Lock ready. The Seattle defense is still just fine, too.

This is a tough game to call. The Chiefs got an easy win over the Broncos. The defense looked good and Kenneth Walker III was outstanding. The passing game still remains an issue. Meanwhile, nothing looked good for the Colts in Week 1. That makes it hard to back them in Week 2 at Arrowhead Stadium. But ugly dogs cover all the time in the NFL.

We shouldn't buy into overreaction. The Rams were -9.5 on the lookahead line. Myles Garrett is great but probably not worth 2.5 points on the line. It seems like this is a good spot to take the Rams and their extra days off since the opener. But we all know that wasn't a normal opener. The Rams supposedly had an aggressive travel plan for Week 1 to avoid the Australia trip taking a toll for weeks after. But what if that's unavoidable? The NFL did neither team any favors shipping them halfway across the world for the season opener and it could linger for them both for a while. Also, the Rams looked terrible in Week 1 and while it's logical to dismiss that due to the long trip, what if it's not? At very least, we need to see the Rams look like the Rams team that was hyped up all offseason before laying a touchdown with them against a Giants team that looked pretty good in the opener. It's amazing what upgrading from Brian Daboll to John Harbaugh can do for a team.

articles.summary: Week 1 was a wacky one in the world of fantasy football, as is often the case. We saw stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Matthew Stafford fall flat, while players like Bryce Young and Jalen Coker shined.
articles.body:
Week 1 was a wacky one in the world of fantasy football, as is often the case. We saw stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Matthew Stafford fall flat, while players like Bryce Young and Jalen Coker shined.

This doesn't mean, of course, that those who disappointed in the opening slate should be avoided in Week 2. Managers should absolutely trust their top draft choices to rebound.

When it comes to second-tier stars, though, it's best to circle the favorable matchups and bypass the tougher challenges. Here, you'll find some start/sit recommendations for point-per-reception (PPR) options in Week 2.

Jalen Hurts and the Philadelphia Eagles offense largely looked average in the debut of new coordinator Sean Mannion. However, Hurts still managed to finish the week as QB8, and he has top-three potential this week.

The Eagles will visit the Tennessee Titans, who operated like the worst team in the NFL in Week 1. The New York Jets racked up 367 yards of offense against the Titans. It wouldn't be a total shock to see Hurts match that total by himself.

The list of other second-tier stars worth considering this week includes:

The Jacksonville Jaguars defense might not be able to match the pressure and opportunistic play we saw from the Kansas City Chiefs' defense on Monday night. However, it's impossible to trust Bo Nix right now against any playoff-caliber unit.

The Denver Broncos are still trying to find their way under new play-caller Davis Webb, and it's likely to be an elongated process.

The Minnesota Vikings used Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason in a split backfield in Week 1, and both backs finished as top-30 RB scorers for the week. Both should be solid flex plays in Week 2, though Mason should get the start for managers who have both rostered.

This week, Mason will face a Chicago Bears defense that was about as solid as a jellyfish in Week 1. Chicago surrendered the seventh-most fantasy points to opposing RBs last week.

Rhamondre Stevenson, New England Patriots

Pittsburgh Steelers running back Jaylen Warren was largely a reliable flex starter in 2025. However, he may not have quite the same value under new head coach Mike McCarthy. He's still Pittsburgh's starter, but he's probably more of a matchup-based option.

Warren finished as RB25 in Week 1, but he'll face a terrific New England Patriots defense on the road this weekend. New England surrendered the seventh-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs last week.

Start: Chris Godwin, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Tampa Bay Buccaneers receiver Chris Godwin looked like his old pre-injury self in Week 1, though he only finished as WR46. He should have a much better statistical outing this week against the visiting Cleveland Browns.

The Browns couldn't cover a twin bed against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1. Now, they'll face a grumpy Baker Mayfield in what he views as a revenge game. Expect Godwin to be targeted early and often.

About the only Browns player worth considering in Week 2 is tight end Harold Fannin Jr. Managers certainly shouldn't trust Jerry Jeudy, who is no longer Cleveland's No. 1 receiver.

The Bucs' defense held Ja'Marr Chase to just two catches and 12 yards last week. Jeudy might end up with negative fantasy points.

New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh brought former Baltimore Ravens tight end Isaiah Likely with him this offseason, and it's clear that Likely is already one of Jaxson Dart's go-to targets. He repeatedly gashed the Dallas Cowboys' defense and finished Week 1 as TE1.

Don't expect Likely to be as productive against a solid Los Angeles Rams defense. Do expect the Giants to pass early and often, which will give Likely a high PPR floor:

Michael Mayer did an admirable job of filling in for Brock Bowers during the Las Vegas Raiders' season-opener. There's a chance that Bowers returns for Week 2, but Mayer shouldn't be trusted regardless.

articles.title: Falcons goofy quarterback drill sparks hilarious reactions from fans on social media
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons' trio of quarterbacks were caught on video hopping backwards like rabbits in a bizarre warm-up drill ahead of the home opener.
articles.body: Just when you thought you'd seen it all when it comes to practice drills on a football field, the Atlanta Falcons decide to put their quarterbacks through a warm-up exercise that one would assume is reserved for ballerinas or cartoon characters. The Falcons welcome the Carolina Panthers to town on Sunday for their home opener, and during practice on Wednesday, the squad's trio of quarterbacks showed off the spring in their steps. Literally. In the video shared across social media, Michael Penix Jr., Cooper Rush, and Jack Strand each take a snap and proceed to take a dropback. The dropbacks, however, aren't exactly typical; instead, the signal callers hop backwards with elongated strides. Penix and Strand appeared to have bought into the drill a bit more than Rush, as they are seen hopping around like rabbits. Rush, who was QB1 for the Falcons' in their season-opening loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers, was going through the motions, and you can't really blame him for doing so. KEVIN STEFANSKI 'NOT RULING ANYBODY OUT' AS INJURIES TO COOPER RUSH, TUA TAGOVAILOA CLOUD FALCONS' QB PLANS In typical fashion, NFL fans had a field day in poking fun at the clip showing the quarterbacks going through the unique drill. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Tua Tagovailoa wasn't a participant during Wednesday's practice in Atlanta as the quarterback continues to deal with an oblique injury. After seeing what the coaching staff put his fellow quarterbacks through on Wednesday, he may be thankful for not being out there. The Falcons were able to be competitive against the Steelers in Week 1 thanks to Bijan Robinson accounting for 173 yards of total offense, but the quarterback situation leaves much to be desired. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Rush finished the contest in Pittsburgh going 12-for-22 in the air for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. Penix, who played in nine games for the Falcons a season ago, did not take a snap against the Steelers and has been limited at practice after undergoing surgery last fall to repair a partially torn ACL. If there is one bright spot from the humiliating warm-up drill, it's that Penix's knee looked to be in great shape.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Leaves Steelers Practice with Trainer amid Contract Talks After Missing Week 1
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. left Thursday's practice with an apparent injury.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. left Thursday's practice with an apparent injury.

The fourth-year defender took part in some portion of the workout before walking off the field with a member of the team's training staff.

2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 2 🏈

A back injury sidelined Porter for Pittsburgh's 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons in Week 1.

This is all coming against the backdrop of the 26-year-old trying to get a new deal. He's headed for free agency in 2027, and Spotrac values him at $23.4 million annually.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported in August that Porter was frustrated with the state of ongoing negotiations, especially since the Steelers locked down others from the 2023 draft class with long-term extensions.

Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported for ESPN on Sept. 13 that a breakthrough is unlikely based on the Steelers' organizational stance on ceasing any negotiations once the season starts.

Pittsburgh listed Porter on its Week 2 injury report but clarified it was down to conditioning and not injury-related. He was limited in Wednesday's practice.

Coach Mike McCarthy struck an optimistic tone Thursday about his level of participation later in the day:

Holdouts are almost prohibitively expensive during training camp by design, and the cost only goes up once the games kick off. Nursing an injury, however, can basically have the same effect without triggering any financial penalties.

It looked like Porter was on track to possibly suit up Sunday against the New England Patriots. Now, his status is harder to pin down.

articles.title: Eagles' Jordan Mailata Calls Out 'Clickbait' After Jeffery Simmons' Comments About Jalen Hurts
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata isn't giving any attention to outside noise going into Sunday's matchup with the Tennessee Titans.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata isn't giving any attention to outside noise going into Sunday's matchup with the Tennessee Titans.

After Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons said earlier in the week that the way to stop Jalen Hurts is to avoid letting him make plays with his legs, Mailata had no response to what he called "clickbait" material:

"I don't pay attention to that stuff. That's clickbait stuff," he said, per The Athletic's Zach Berman . "That's what you guys get paid for. ...I only care about everyone in this locker room. This locker room is all I give a damn about it. I don't care what you guys say about this locker room, I don't care what any other locker room says about this locker room. This is my focus."

Simmons' exact quote was the Titans need to make Hurts "be a quarterback" to "Stop his runs, make sure (he) doesn't get out of the pocket and make plays."

It reads like a fairly innocuous comment, but given how much discussion there has been over the past 12 months about Hurts and the Eagles' passing game, it could be interpreted as a dig at his pocket presence.

There are people in the NFL who would agree with Simmons' assessment that keeping Hurts in the pocket is the best way to defend him.

In the quarterback tiers column from The Athletic's Mike Sando that posted on Aug. 4, one defensive coach talking about Hurts said his "best plays are off schedule."

Hurts had an up-and-down performance in Week 1 against the Washington Commanders. He finished 14-of-25 for 203 yards and three touchdowns, along with 46 rushing yards on seven carries.

The Eagles' first three possessions in the second half ended in three-and-outs, but those were followed by back-to-back scoring drives, including a 43-yard touchdown pass from Hurts to Dallas Goedert that was the difference in the game.

There will probably always be a high variance in Hurts' play on a possession-to-possession basis, but the overall results for the Eagles with him as their starting quarterback have been strong enough to produce one Super Bowl victory in two trips to the big game.

articles.title: Giants’ run game will be a major test for the Rams
articles.summary: LA gave up the fourth-most rushing yards in the league in Week 1
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams were poor across the board in Week 1, but especially against the run, nearly giving up 200 yards to the 49ers. With New York coming to town, the Giants ' running game will pose one of the tougher challenges to the Rams' iffy run defense this season.

In the 20-point season-opening loss, LA gave up the fourth-most rushing yards in the NFL at 174, behind the Panthers (291), Broncos (220) and Colts (202). While the defense didn't give up a 100-yard rusher, they still allowed Niners running back Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black to rush for at least 65 yards.

Things must tighten up quickly, or the Rams risk being run out of their own stadium against an unexpectedly physical Giants attack.

New York rushed for 165 yards against a supposedly improved Dallas defensive front, fifth-most in the league in Week 1. Second-year running back Cam Skattebo led the way with 81 yards on 18 carries. The offense also has plenty of mouths to feed at RB.

Veteran Devin Singletary is closing in on 5,000 career rushing yards through his first seven seasons. Third-year back Tyrone Tracy Jr. is coming off back-to-back 740+ yard campaigns. The trio of Skattebo, Singletary and Tracy combined for 1,587 yards last season. That is remarkable production at its finest, and is exactly why the team finished fifth in rushing a year ago.

How effective was their ground attack? NY currently has the lowest rate of runs stuffed in the NFL. The Giants violently barrel down people like they're owed lunch money, which bodes well for the run game, proving so far that it '25 was no fluke, even with a different coaching staff. What's crazier is that the unit could actually improve as the season progresses.

A powerful run game defines a John Harbaugh offense, dating back to his Ravens tenure. From 2008 to 2025, Baltimore averaged an NFL-leading 139.8 rushing yards per game, which was 10 yards more than the second-best team, according to the Giants team website . Additionally, the Ravens led the NFL in rushing yards five times in their last seven seasons, including 2019, 2020, 2023, 2024 and 2025.

So, the G-Men will be running the ball plenty on Monday night. Now the question becomes whether the Rams can stop it when they know it's coming.

Run defense woes reared their ugly head in Week 1

The Rams had seemingly made strides against the run in 2025, but experienced lapses towards the end of the season.

Los Angeles gave up eight 100-yard rushing games last season, which, overall, isn't bad. However, five of those games came after the team's bye, including the Falcons piling up a staggering 219 yards in Week 17.

During LA's 17-3 win over Harbaugh's Ravens in October 2025, Baltimore racked up 179 yards on the ground, the second-most the Rams had given up after the Atlanta game. That total came without two-time MVP Lamar Jackson out of the lineup due to injury. Had Jackson played, the Ravens could've easily gone over 200 rushing yards.

The bleeding didn't exactly stop in the playoffs, even if LA had allowed one opponent to amass well over 100 team rushing yards (Bears, 160). In total, the Rams gave up 318 rushing yards and four touchdowns in three games.

Between the regular season and playoffs, the team gave up 100-yard games in nearly half of its 20 games played. Two-thirds of that came after their bye alone. Clearly, the Rams have adjustments to make in their run defense, as they reverted to the inconsistent play that plagued them in the back half of last season.

Knowing full well what Harbaugh and the Giants intend to do this week, LA must be better prepared than it was against the Niners, given that New York poses one of the tougher challenges to the Rams on the ground this season.
