articles.title: Cowboys' Quinnen Williams Says He's 'Got to Do Better' After Assessing Performance in Loss to Giants
articles.summary: After a lackluster performance in the Dallas Cowboys' Week 1 loss against the New York Giants, star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams knows he needs to make more of an impact for the team to be successful.
articles.body:
After a lackluster performance in the Dallas Cowboys' Week 1 loss against the New York Giants, star defensive tackle Quinnen Williams knows he needs to make more of an impact for the team to be successful.

Williams told team reporter Tommy Yarrish that he wasn't pleased with his performance against the Giants, and he's motivated to return to his usual self.

"No, not at all man," Williams said. "Can't nobody in this world hold me accountable more than I hold myself. Can't nobody in this world critique me more than myself. So I expect to be dominant every single week, I expect to be a playmaker or a game changer every single week. I wasn't that, and I got to do better."

Williams finished with just three tackles in Dallas' 28-20 loss against a New York team that is still completing a rebuild under first-year head coach John Harbaugh.

A Pro Bowl selection in each of the last four years, Williams was rewarded with a three-year, $105.9 million extension this offseason that made him the second-highest-paid defensive tackle in the NFL. The Cowboys gave up a 2025 second-round pick and the higher of their two first-rounders this year to acquire him from the New York Jets, so he will have to produce in a big way to live up to expectations.

Williams will try to bounce back when the Cowboys return to action on Sunday against the Washington Commanders.

articles.title: Cowboys DC Christian Parker addresses viral video of talk with rookie
articles.summary: A video of a sideline discussion between Cowboys rookie Jaishawn Barham and defensive coordinator Christian Parker went viral after Dallas' loss.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys' season-opening loss to the New York Giants necessitated several conversations about the breakdowns that plagued a defense trying to move on from last year, when it surrendered more points than any other unit in the NFL.

One such summit occurred during the game.

On Wednesday, Sept. 16, a video of a sideline interaction between Cowboys rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham and first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker was spread wide on social media. Barham looked ahead as Parker, who sat next to him, spoke with him. Barham then stood up and walked away with fellow linebacker DeMarvion Overshown .

One day later, Parker broke down the interaction, which he said was driven by the rookie's frustration.

"It was his first NFL game. Things aren't going to be perfect," Parker said in a news conference. "This isn't a fairy tale at all. Jaishawn cares as much as anybody in that locker room about us winning, No. 1, but No. 2 our defensive performance."

Parker added that the team had no concerns about Barham's passion or level of dedication.

"I don't think anyone in our building has any doubt about what he's gonna do coming real soon," Parker sad. "We don't have any reservations about his mentality. We welcome that passion. Have to channel it better. That's something that young players have to go through. It's a natural progression."

A third-round pick out of Michigan, Barham played in 49% of the Cowboys' defensive snaps in the 28-20 loss to the Giants . He collected five tackles in his debut yet earned an unwanted spotlight in the fourth quarter. He appeared to pull up while in pursuit of running back Devin Singletary , who took a pass to the flat into the end zone for a 9-yard touchdown.

New York racked up 29 first downs on the night and converted 9 of 11 third downs.

The Cowboys face the Washington Commanders on Sunday in Week 2.

articles.title: College Fantasy Football Week 3 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: What to do with Amare Thomas, Jordan Marshall, more
articles.summary: College fantasy analyst Eric Froton offers start/sit advice for your Week 3 lineups.
articles.body:
The college fantasy football landscape is rapidly changing due to injuries and depth chart movement. With some huge matchups set to kickoff this weekend, here are my Week 3 Start/Sit recommendations.

Faizon Brandon, Tennessee vs. Kennesaw State

True freshman Faizon Brandon flashed his massive upside in the season opener against FCS Furman, lighting up the Paladins for 226 passing yards and three touchdown passes while rolling up 68 rushing yards and two rushing scores for a robust 39.8 Yahoo fantasy points. Tennessee HC Josh Heupel noted that Brandon displayed "poise and control" after his first 45-24 road win against Georgia Tech , where the QB completed just 10-of-21 passes for 16.1 fantasy points as UT recorded a dominant 299 rushing yards. He has been very effective downfield, completing 7-of-11 passes of 11+ yards with all five of his passing touchdowns occurring in the mid-to-long range. This week's tune-up versus a lower-echelon G6 program Kennesaw State is Heupel's last chance to get Brandon a live-action confidence boost with a home showdown against SEC juggernaut Texas on tap in Week 4. I think we see a reprieve of Faizon's explosion against Furman, which should lead to another 30+ fantasy points for the promising freshman, making him a quality streaming option this week.

Becht has a high floor in this lopsided matchup against a porous Buffalo defense that is allowing 18.7 yards per successful dropback (132nd) with 20% of passes defended being 20+ yards downfield. He has thrown seven touchdowns with zero interceptions in Penn State's first two games and is an extremely safe bet for another 3+ TD passes.

Georgia has done literally whatever they want through their first two games, scoring 133 points against hapless Tennessee State and Western Kentucky . Stockton has thrown eight touchdowns and effortlessly cruised down the field against each team before hitting the showers at halftime. He now should play his first full game and cross the 25-point barrier against SEC opponent Arkansas, who just got clobbered 43-10 by Utah.

Sheppard has taken the college fantasy football world by storm as he leads the P4 with 374 rushing yards on 6.3 YPC with an eye popping 25.4% of his carries going for 10+ yards. With the Blue Devils losing irreplaceable QB Darian Mensah (Miami) and their top-two WRs Cooper Barkate (Miami) and Que'Sean Brown ( Virginia Tech ), Sheppard has become the focal point of OC Jonathan Brewer's offense, which is running the ball 69% of the time on standard downs (20th in FBS) and leads the nation with 46.2% of the team's pass attempts being thrown to players running routes out of the backfield.

Sheppard hasn't just feasted on lower-level opponents either, facing perennial G6 stalwart Tulane (17-3 win) and Big Ten foe Illinois on the road (31-27 win). Sheppard will be keyed on again this week as Duke opens its ACC schedule against a leaky Stanford defense that has allowed a 46.5% success rate (123rd) and is allowing 36.0 PPG through two games. He is my Week 3 fantasy RB1 and should be started in all formats.

I unleashed a certified campaign in the offseason letting anyone who would listen to me know that Jadan Baugh is the RB1 of the 2027 NFL Draft and has a legitimate shot at leading the nation in rushing yards. He is a matchup-proof, must-start in all formats going forward until further notice. Think Marshawn Lynch-lite.

Parker has made up for his lack of goal-line equity last year by scoring an absurd six total touchdowns with eight receptions for a gaudy 30.6 fantasy PPG average. Utah OC Kevin McGiven led the Utah State offense last season and should have little trouble dissecting the Aggies defense that allowed 29 points to Idaho State.

Despite looking dynamic handling 25 carries for 142 yards with 5 receptions against UNC in Week 1, and TCU scoring 63 points against Grambling last week, Payne still hasn't scored a touchdown. He should easily top 100-yards and find the end zone against Arkansas State's pitiful run defense that is allowing 2.90 yards before contact (132nd in FBS).

You might be tempted to bench Thomas since Houston is going up against the seemingly mythical Texas Tech defense that smothered every offense in their wake last year. However, several key cogs of the Red Raiders' D are now in the NFL leaving DC Shiel Wood to work with an objectively less-talented group this season. The talent disparity showed up last week with Oregon State's rising QB Brady Atkinson lighting up the TT secondary for 399 yards and two touchdowns. He connected with the hottest freshman WR in the country, Jesse Legree, who caught eight passes for a sensational 240 yards and two touchdowns.

OSU's explosion bodes well for Houston's volume hog Thomas, who is commanding 32% of Houston's targets with 73% of his receptions gaining first down yardage after averaging a sterling 15.1 PPG in 2025. Don't be fooled into benching Thomas in this pivotal Big 12 showdown, as Houston will need to throw to keep pace with Texas Tech in what projects to be a very aggressive game script.

The most explosive receiver in the 28-year history of Kirk Ferentz's Hawkeye tenure, Diaz has received 25 targets and one designed run, which he has converted into 189 total yards and a touchdown for 16.2 PPG. Diaz should find the end zone again, as he will have to pick up the slack for injured star TE DJ Vonnahme .

Omarion Miller , Arizona State at Kansas

Miller erupted for eight catches, 102 yards and a touchdown in Week 1 before posting one of the strangest stat lines of Week 2, turning 16 targets into nine receptions for just 29 yards. He should once again score double-digit fantasy points against a vulnerable Kansas secondary.

Few P4 wideouts have seen a meteoric rise like Olugbode, as secured at least six receptions for 100+ and a touchdown in each of his first two contests. He should feast on an overmatched Troy secondary.

Luke Reynolds , Virginia Tech at Maryland

I had the opportunity to watch the Massachusetts native completely dominate the Elite 11 Finals and display a noticeable chemistry with his now college QB at Virginia Tech, Ethan Grunkemeyer . The two emerging juniors are leading an aggressive Virginia Tech passing attack that is averaging 339 yards per game with 41% of team pass attempts being wide open (eighth in FBS).

New HC James Franklin has the Hokies throwing at top-25 rates on both standard and passing downs which reflects the trust he has in the cerebral Grunkemeyer who started seven games in 2025 for Penn State in relief of Drew Allar , winning his last four starts. For his part, Reynolds has been a force to be reckoned with, averaging 20.1 half-PPR fantasy points per game which ranks No. 1 the nation amongst his fellow tight ends. Reynolds leads the team in targets, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, and is expected to receive another eight-target workload this weekend against an up-tempo Maryland team that should breed a competitive environment with plenty of aerial action.

Bowman is the unquestioned freshman Tight End of the Year so far this season, as he broke out in a huge way with six receptions for 83 yards and two touchdowns last week versus Louisiana . He has the pleasure of facing a Rutgers team that fielded the most generous fantasy defense in the entire P4 last year, and he should feast once again.

Beers was listed behind blocking TE Hayden Hansen on the initial depth chart, but has taken over Jaren Kanak's high-target flex-TE role that garnered him nine targets for 94 yards last week vs. Michigan . With QB John Mateer struggling to throw outside the hashes, expect Beers to have another strong game against New Mexico this week.

It's hard to believe that the same Will Hammond who averaged 7.0 yards per carry while rushing for 299 yards and five rushing scores through nine games is the same QB who has run for -11 yards on eight carries against Abilene Christian and Oregon State. Hammond suffered a season ending knee ligament tear that required surgery to repair. His recovery timetable was rushed when the Sorsby fiasco unfolded, leaving Hammond as the only true startable option in the Tech QB room until a court ruling allowed former Florida State dual-threat quarterback Thomas Castellanos to join the team in late-August.

Castellanos did not play in Week 1 but was instrumental in Tech's 35-24 victory over Oregon State, throwing an eight-yard touchdown pass and running five times for 15 yards and another touchdown on the ground. HC Joey Maguire lauded Castellanos for being "dangerous with the ball in his hands" and vowed to involve Castellanos more in the offense. Such positive news is catastrophic for Hammond's CFF value, and positions Castellanos to potentially take over the starting job if Hammond can't perform to expectations. Hammond is a must-sit in Week 3 and will be extremely tough to trust in a college fantasy context going forward.

Leavitt is questionable/doubtful to play at Ole Miss, so even if he does suit up the possibility of an early exit in a heated rivalry game is enough to exercise caution and bench Leavitt at The Grove.

Jackson looked completely overmatched in a cross-country, non-conference matchup against Utah last weekend, and is in line to be replaced by four-star backup QB AJ Hill if he starts slowly against Georgia's rugged defense.

Jordan Marshall , Michigan vs. New Mexico

Michigan is somehow 2-0 despite scoring just 30 points in two games and needing one of the most controversial game clock rulings in modern history to defeat Western Michigan 13-12. The Wolverines have converted just 7-of-23 third downs and rank a dismal 127th in rushing success rate, as they have gone 3-and-out a shocking 43% of the time (129th in FBS). Starting RB Jordan Marshall took over the lead rushing duties last year after Justice Haynes went down with an injury, running for 932 rushing yards, 6.2 YPC and 10 touchdowns for a respectable 15.6 fantasy PPG.

However, Marshall is splitting carries with five-star freshman phenom Savion Hiter, who looks dynamic and ready to be a major contributor in the passing game right out of the gate, securing all four of his targets for 40 yards. The struggles of QB Bryce Underwood have been well documented in derailing UM's ability to move the ball down the field as well, allowing defenses to stack 7-8 men in the box and dare Underwood to beat them vertically. The result has been to run Underwood 24 times for a team-leading 145 rushing yards, which has marginalized Marshall's role in the offense. Marshall carried a second-round ADP in Yahoo leagues this offseason, but his diminished usage profile and modest 8.2 fantasy points per game make him a sit in Week 3 as Michigan flails to correct their sputtering offense.

Raphael was a volume hog with Cal last season, logging 233 carries with 34 receptions for the Bears. However at SMU he is splitting carries with Dramekco Green and third-down back Derrick McFall which limits his CFF appeal.

Jackson has been able to sustain some fantasy appeal via his six receptions for 96 yards and two touchdown receptions in lopsided victories. However, Rodney Fields is the clear RB1, which means a fall off is on the horizon for RB2 Jackson.

It has been a precipitous fall for Dickey, who has gone from Texas Tech's bell cow last season to being on the short-side of a three-way committee alongside J'Koby Williams and Quinten Joyner . He is unstartable until further notice.

SMU HC Rhett Lashlee had fantasy enthusiasts salivating at the idea of a " James Proche type season" for the shifty slot receiver Yamir Knight. The preseason hype helped to vault Knight into the top-35 of P4 wideouts according to Yahoo ADP, but that optimism has faded after two middling performances to open the season. The Mustangs have spread the ball around to a dizzying degree, with 14 different players catching at least two passes thus far.

While he leads the team with 11 targets his usage reflects a typical slot profile, with the diminutive (5'8"/185 lbs) Knight commanding a modest 4.6 average depth of target and ranking fourth on the team in receiving yardage while securing zero of SMU's 10 receiving touchdowns. Knight is an effective chain-mover between the 20's, but he's a relative ghost in red zone situations which limits his fantasy utility. SMU faces a strong Louisville defense that is allowing a solid 58% completion rate and 35% passing success rate despite facing Ole Miss and star QB Trinidad Chambliss . Knight's limited route tree and lack of red zone usage means you should leave him on your bench in this tough ACC road showdown.

I had my reservations about Wesco heading into the year due to his poor ball-tracking and boom/bust profile. But even I could predict his dismal 67 total yards Wesco has produced thus far. Thrown in true freshman run-first QB Tait Reynolds, and Wesco simply cannot be trusted in your lineup this week.

Nyck Harbor , South Carolina vs. Mississippi State

Somehow, Harbor has only accrued 105 receiving yards and zero scores despite SC scoring 102 points against helpless opponents. It's feast or famine with Harbor, so bench him until we see him justify a starting lineup spot.

While Marshall is the primary target for Arkansas, catching 12 passes for 142 yards in his first two games, it is impossible to trust Arkansas' limping offense that is going to get crushed by Georgia.

Oakley was a hot commodity in the offseason after recording 38 receptions for 389 yards and six touchdowns last year, boasting 13 total touchdown receptions in his three years with the Wildcats. However, that was under former HC Chris Kleiman who preferred to target his tight ends much more often than new HC Collin Klein. Thus far, Oakley has been reduced to a safety valve, catching two of four targets for 40 yards and zero touchdowns despite Kansas State ringing up 105 points and 439 passing yards overall. KSU has relied heavily on the ground game, gashing their two non-conference opponents for 607 rushing yards with a 60% run rate on standard downs.

The team's target distribution has focused heavily on the receivers and running backs, as 37 of Kansas State's 41 receptions have gone to non-tight ends. Toss in the fact Oakley dropped 12 passes heading into the year, and he's already dropped one of this four targets this season, and Oakley is a risky start against a Tulane team that Kansas State is favored over by 20.5 points, and Oakley projects as a low-volume, touchdown dependent college fantasy option who will need to score in the first half in case KSU puts their starters on ice in the third-quarter.

There were hopes Lofton could inherit a target share similar to former Miami TE Elijah Arroyo , however that dream has been shattered after Lofton received just two targets for 23 yards in Miami's first two contests.

A consensus top-five preseason TE, Wade has seen his CFF value plummet after catching just three passes for 35 yards in UCF's first two games. Toss in the fact starting QB Alonza Barnett is expected to miss the next few weeks, and Wade simply cannot be trusted.

articles.title: Paperwork for permanent seal of evidence in Josh Jacobs case resubmitted
articles.summary: Due to a formatting issue, the victim’s motion for a permanent seal of evidence must be refiled with the Judge Marc Hammer
articles.body:
The victim in Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs' legal matter requested a permanent seal of discovery evidence after Jacobs pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal damage to property last week. According to FOX 11 News in Green Bay , Judge Marc Hammer, who is overseeing this case, denied the victim's motion for a permanent seal due to a paperwork issue. Per the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel , the request was "not in the proper format for the Brown County court system," and the judge encouraged her legal team to refile the request.

According to the documents provided to FOX 11 News, the motion was declined on Tuesday and was officially filed on Thursday.

Below was the justification for keeping evidence from entering the public sphere, from the perspective of the victim's representation:

The Court finds that public disclosure of the Discovery Material would threaten or substantially impair ANM's privacy, dignity, personal security, emotional well-being, or ability to participate safely in the criminal-justice process. This protection is not to impede any legitimate law-enforcement function, criminal prosecution, judicial proceeding, or disclosure otherwise required by law, but to prevent unnecessary public dissemination of information that identifies ANM, reveals intimate or sensitive details of ANM, or creates a material risk of harm.

ANM is an acronym used for the anonymous woman identified as Jacobs' girlfriend.

At the moment, the next hearing in this case — where we might see the judge making a ruling on the refiled paperwork from victim's team — is set to overlap with the same day as a nationally televised Packers game, as Green Bay will host their first home game of the year against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday, September 24th.

Evidence, particularly a video, is becoming a crucial piece of this story, as the police report stated that a forensics analysis team was able to recover footage from a camera in Jacobs' garage that shows part of "the altercation." Per the police report, the running back "grabbed [victim] and threw her to the ground and she struck her head" while she tried to leave Jacobs' residence via the garage after a dispute that originated over text messages.

The police report states flatly that she is seen on the ground in the garage and that "approximately 40 seconds later, Jacobs returns to the garage and appears to damage ANM's phone." What is unclear, because of the wording of the police report, is whether or not "the altercation" includes the portion of the dispute where Jacobs had a physical interaction with his girlfriend.

Fueling the fire for interest in the video is that the NFL is reportedly attempting to acquire the video prior to making a ruling on Jacobs' return to the field. At the moment, Jacobs is on the commissioner exempt list, essentially a purgatory situation as it stands right now. He's not officially suspended by the league, and any time on the commissioner exempt list will essentially function as time served toward a suspension — if the NFL suspends him — but the league has yet to make a decision on whether they will suspend Jacobs or for how long.

Jacobs' legal team asked for a temporary order to seal evidence , which is why the video evidence is still sealed today. For whatever it's worth, Jacobs' request was filed on September 10th — the day of his no contest plea — while the victim's original request was filed on September 15th. Below was the justification that Jacobs' representatives filed with the court for the evidence being sealed:

The Court finds that public disclosure of the Discovery Material would threaten or substantially impair Defendant's and [the victim's] privacy, dignity, personal security, emotional wellbeing, or ability to participate safely in the criminal-justice process. This protection is not to impede any legitimate law-enforcement function, criminal prosecution judicial proceeding, or disclosure otherwise required by law, but to prevent unnecessary public dissemination of information that identifies [the victim], reveals intimate or sensitive details of [the victim] or the Defendant, or creates a material risk of harm.

The timing of the NFL's punishment for Jacobs and the potential release of a video is important to the league, as Ray Rice took the NFL to arbitration over his indefinite suspension in 2014. Initially, the league only suspended Rice for two games, but after the video of his domestic violence incident went public, the NFL pushed him more severely. In the end, it was ruled that the league only had one opportunity to suspend the running back for a single personal conduct violation, because Rice never misled the NFL, and he was paid back for the game checks that he missed while on suspension.

The NFL learned the hard way back in 2014 that they only get to use the suspension button once per case, as long as they aren't misled, and can't just use the temperature of public perception to a video to justify added punishment. Because of that Rice ruling in 2014 and the situation surrounding the video evidence in this case, the league's announcement of a potential Jacobs suspension is taking some time.

Update: The lawyers for the victim have resubmitted their proposal, according to WBAY in Green Bay .

articles.title: Saints' Tyler Shough Compared to 'Poor Man's Josh Allen' by Ravens DC Anthony Weaver
articles.summary: Heading into their matchup on Sunday with the New Orleans Saints, Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver had high praise for Tyler Shough.
articles.body:
Heading into their matchup on Sunday with the New Orleans Saints, Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver had high praise for Tyler Shough.

Weaver told reporters on Thursday that Shough reminds him of a "poor man's Josh Allen" and the "sky's the limit" for the Saints quarterback.

Shough was one of the most interesting prospects in recent memory leading up to the 2025 draft. He was well regarded by many analysts, but no one seemed to know how to properly rank him since he turned 26 early in his rookie season.

Allen, who turned 22 one month after he was selected No. 7 overall by the Buffalo Bills in the 2018 draft, was regarded as a developmental prospect coming out of Wyoming.

There are some physical comparisons between Shough and Allen. Shough measured in at 6'5" and 219 pounds with a 32-inch vertical jump and a 9'9" broad jump.

Allen was listed just under 6'5" and 237 pounds with a 33.5-inch vertical jump and a 9'11" broad jump.

Even though Shough's age was held against him, he has looked pretty good since taking over as New Orleans' starting quarterback. He threw for 2,384 yards, 10 touchdowns, six interceptions and ran for 186 yards with three scores on 45 carries in 11 appearances (nine starts) as a rookie.

From a pure statistical standpoint, Shough was a better passer than Allen as a rookie. Allen threw for 2,074 yards, 10 touchdowns, 12 interceptions in 12 games during the 2018 season. He did have a huge edge on the ground with 631 yards and eight touchdowns on 89 rushing attempts.

It took Allen until his third season before he married the elite-level passing with his ability to run the football.

Shough threw for 410 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions in Week 1 against the Detroit Lions.

The Saints scored all 30 points in that game after halftime. They had a chance to win in overtime, but Shough's two-point conversion pass to Bryce Lance was incomplete.

No one will argue Shough is close to Allen right now, but their physical profiles do suggest the Saints quarterback could become a better NFL player than anyone thought when most of the focus was on his draft age.

articles.title: NFL's Oldest and Youngest Rosters Revealed After Week 1 Games, Full Team-By-Team Breakdown
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are starting off the 2026 season as the oldest team in the NFL.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are starting off the 2026 season as the oldest team in the NFL.

The Niners' Week 1 roster boasted a league-high average age of around 27 and a half years old, according to the NFL .

That's more than two years older than the average age of the Miami Dolphins, which ranked as the NFL's youngest roster in Week 1.

Here's a look at the full breakdown of NFL roster ages from youngest to oldest heading into Week 2 of the 2026 season, courtesy of the NFL.

The Dolphins came in at the low end of the average age rankings in large part of their NFL-high rookie class of 15 first-year players including first-round pick Kadyn Proctor.

The Los Angeles Rams, which rank as one of the NFL's oldest teams, are in contrast beginning the campaign with a veteran roster featuring just three rookies.

The Pittsburgh Steelers lead the NFL in players aged 30 or older with 12 players on their roster, including starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, fitting the bill.

The NFL's average age sits right around 26 and a half years old to begin the season, according to the league.

Week 2 kicks off Thursday night with a matchup between two rosters sitting right around that league average in the Detroit Lions and Buffalo Bills. Both teams are looking to start the season 2-0 after kicking off at 8:15 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium.

If you live in Florida long enough, you just get a feel for these things. A sixth sense. We know the difference between 90 and 85. When the mornings are 76 and not 86, we can immediately feel it. BET365 BONUS CODE: BET $10, GET $365 WIN OR LOSE ON THURSDAY NIGHT FOOTBALL, BILLS VS LIONS This morning was one of those mornings. I can't wait to see what tonight holds. Let's roll. The response was so big, I think I'm going to turn it into a column later this week. I'll give you a taste today, though. For those who don't know, the cheeseburger from Buffalo Wild Wings is, without a doubt, the best burger in America. I've stood on this hill for years now, and I feel as strong today as I ever have. Unfortunately, we went to Applebee's this year for the draft, and — while good — their burger didn't even come close. I also started 0-1 last week, which can't be a coincidence. We'll see how this week goes. OK, enough food talk. Let's get this class going with Paige Spiranac saying goodbye to summer with a bikini-clad Instagram post, and then defending Sydney Sweeney in the comments section. Naturally. Landry Kiffin claps back at the haters "God forbid a woman loves her nice cans." Put it on a hat, Paige! She's the influencer who started all of this, right? Paige Spiranac walked so everyone else could run. Influencers nowadays are a dime a dozen. They're everywhere. When Paige Spiranac first started out, she was it. So when Paige chimes in on something, we listen. And she stated the obvious about this whole Sydney Sweeney drama ... THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! It's nonsense. Complete and total nonsense. I'd wager a guess that Novig has seen a 100% increase in sign-ups since Sydney launched her new campaign. That's a win. "Oh no, she lost 200,000 of her Instagram followers!" Give me a break. Have any of them hit a 7-player prop parlay that pays $1,300? Don't think so. That's all that matters. OK, let's move this class along and check in on Landry Kiffin, who has, allegedly, been the subject of some NASTY signage up and down Oxford this week ahead of her dad's big return: I'll never forgive CBS & you guys brought it STRONG this week "I understand emotions are high this week, and people are upset, but I’m my own person," Kiffin said, adding that she's been the "punchline" of a sexual joke. "I’ll never understand how someone can feel good about themselves putting such vulgar things about a girl on a giant banner hanging from their house." Landry went on to say that students are "saying really inappropriate things about me with somebody I genuinely have never met in my life, which makes it even more frustrating," and that she hopes "people realize there is an actual person behind the jokes people make." All of this stems from a rumor in Oxford — a long-running rumor, I might add — that Landry Kiffin and a former player had sexual relations during Lane Kiffin's tenure at Ole Miss. Fans believe that is the reason this former player was essentially benched last season. I don't feel like getting a call from Legal today, so I won't go into further detail. Feel free to Google it on your own time. It ain't hard to find. Anyway, Landry is still a student at Ole Miss, which really makes this feel like some serious friendly fire to me. Tensions are HIGH in Oxford right now. I can't wait for Saturday night. Game of the Year, by a mile. OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big night of Al Michaels and Kirk Herbstreit. Speaking of that Ole Miss-LSU game, you know what channel it should be on? CBS. This came across my desk this morning, and buddy, it made me feel so many things: Lordy. I miss the SEC on CBS so much, it hurts. That's my childhood. That song, and that intro, and those announcers ... it's all my childhood. Nothing will ever come close. For those wondering how CBS's new deal with the Big Ten is working out ... the marquee game this weekend? USC at Rutgers. What a fall from grace. Next? Yesterday I asked if we had any former UF students who were on campus/in school during the infamous 1990 season when the Gainesville Ripper was on the loose. Like I said, I'm going to go further in depth later this week. Just wild stuff. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If anyone else has any stories, please, reach out. I'm all ears. articles.title: Detroit Lions vs Buffalo Bills Thursday Night Football preview and betting odds for Week 2
articles.summary: Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills host the Detroit Lions in a Thursday Night Football showdown after both teams survived dramatic Week 1 victories.
articles.body: Thursday Night Football is back for us, and we are ready to start betting on yet another week of the NFL. Week 1 went okay, and as we get more information, we should get even better and bigger plays to put our money on. Over the years, Thursday night games have been better matchups. Before, they used to be ones that you’d barely care about because they were between bad teams. This has the makings of a great matchup between the Lions and Bills. The Detroit Lions like to make things difficult for themselves, don’t they? Despite the odd victory in Week 1, they still are 1-0, which is better than half of the teams in the league. The Lions were ahead in the third quarter by 21 points, but they let the Saints march all the way back and tie the game. Then the game went into overtime, where Detroit looked great on offense. They had a chance to end the game on a fourth down. It did not work out, as the Saints converted. The Lions' defense was one of the main problems; they couldn’t get off the field when they needed. However, they did stop the 2-point conversion that would’ve lost them the game. The Saints weren’t even in a hurry-up offense when the Lions were struggling. That’s what makes me the most concerned about the team overall. On offense, Jahmyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown looked great in the game, both scoring two touchdowns. LIONS AVOID FRANCHISE-WORST COLLAPSE AS DEFENSE STOPS SAINTS TWO-POINT CONVERSION IN OT The Buffalo Bills are another team that really doesn’t take the easy way out. It is almost like they look at Josh Allen and say, "Try and beat us, just don’t let this guy get the ball with a chance to win the game." Sure, sometimes it doesn’t work out, and it never does in the postseason. However, the strategy does seem to get them to double-digit wins each year. The Bills were able to get a solid 36-31 victory over the Texans to open their season. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Houston was expected to have one of the best defenses in the game, and Allen and company carved them up. Allen threw for 334 yards with two touchdowns, and added another two touchdowns on the ground while running for 23 yards. It seems like he liked his new target DJ Moore, who hauled in five receptions for 100 yards and a score. The Bills defense, one of the downfalls, did get the stop needed in this one and held off a late scoring drive. NFL WEEK 1 TAKEAWAYS: BENGALS FLASH CONTENDER UPSIDE, BEARS EXPLODE AND PACKERS COLLAPSE Based on the scoring from the first game, the Bills and Lions should rack up points in this one. The line has already moved higher, but that may be a bit of an overreaction to the first week’s scoring. I think this game goes under the total. Thursday night games tend to be a bit lower scoring. I also am not confident that the new field for the Bills is in great shape after they had to redo it. Finally, I think both teams will make the adjustments on defense more than offense. I’m going to back the under 54.5. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER For more sports betting information and plays, follow David on X/Twitter: @futureprez2024

articles.title: Mike McDaniel Says 'It Would Be Cool' if Maxx Crosby 'Wanted to Take a Nap' for Chargers vs. Raiders
articles.summary: Mike McDaniel is hoping to avoid a heavy dose of Maxx Crosby this week.
articles.body:
Mike McDaniel is hoping to avoid a heavy dose of Maxx Crosby this week.

The Los Angeles Chargers' offensive coordinator joked that he wishes the Las Vegas Raiders edge rusher would "take a nap" during this Sunday's clash between the two teams.

"He is relentless and I enjoy the challenge, but it would be cool if he was tired and wanted to take a nap," McDaniel told reporters on Thursday.

Crosby is a force to be reckoned with every time he steps on the field, so it's hard to blame McDaniel for wanting him to take it easy. The defensive end started his season off right in Week 1, picking up two tackles and 1.5 sacks in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins.

Crosby, 29, had a productive season in 2025 despite the Raiders' struggles, logging 73 tackles, 10 sacks, six passes defended, two forced fumbles and an interception.

During the offseason, he appeared to be on his way to Baltimore before the Ravens backed out of the deal . Offensive coordinators in the AFC West rejoiced for a moment before the five-time Pro Bowler returned to Las Vegas.

The Chargers appeared to be sleeper Super Bowl contenders coming into the season, but an upset loss to the Arizona Cardinals has perhaps tempered expectations.

Among the issues in that game was Los Angeles' offensive line, which allowed three sacks and five quarterback hits to Justin Herbert.

"You have a lot of visions coming to a new team and working on something for months — and the vision never looked like that," McDaniel told reporters of his first game as the Chargers' OC. "It was a case of humble pie. Didn't feel good to anyone."

It only gets more difficult this week going up against a Raiders team that recorded five sacks, 11 quarterback hits and an interception in last week's game.

The Chargers are 6.5-point favorites against the Raiders, per FanDuel Sportsbook , but it wouldn't be surprising to see Las Vegas put up a fight.

articles.title: Ravens worked out Brandin Cooks on Thursday
articles.summary: With Zay Flowers dealing with a hamstring injury and Ja'Kobi Lane on IR with a fractured wrist, the Ravens are looking for some help at receiver.
articles.body:
With Zay Flowers dealing with a hamstring injury and Ja'Kobi Lane on IR with a fractured wrist, the Ravens are looking for some help at receiver.

According to the league's daily transaction wire, Brandin Cooks worked out for Baltimore on Thursday.

Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports no signing is imminent, but Cooks could be an option for the club moving forward.

Cooks, who turns 33 later this month, appeared in 15 total games with five starts last year. He began the season with New Orleans , catching 19 passes for 165 yards. He then went to Buffalo where he had five receptions for 114 yards in five regular-season games.

He then had five catches for 78 yards for the Bills in the postseason. But he infamously didn't handle a downfield overtime throw from Josh Allen in the divisional round, leading to an interception and an eventual loss to Denver .

Cooks has appeared in 173 games with 149 starts since being selected at No. 20 overall in the 2014 draft. He's caught 734 passes for 9,811 yards with 60 touchdowns for the Saints, Patriots, Rams, Texans, Cowboys, and Bills.

articles.title: NFL betting, odds, lines: Betting trends to know for Week 2's biggest games
articles.summary: Here are a few betting trends to help you with your wagers in Week 2.
articles.body:
The opening week of the 2026 season yielded mixed results in the NFL betting trends department.

On one hand, the Bengals , Bears and Giants — all notoriously slow starters in recent years — won and covered in Week 1.

Also, Houston 's nine-game overall and seven-game home winning streaks ended against the Bills. The Rams fell for just the ninth time in their last 30 regular season games. And Tampa Bay dropped its first season opener since 2020 (falling in Cincinnati ).

Then again, Jacksonville (9-0 SU and ATS regular season run), Seattle (11 straight victories, including the playoffs) and Minnesota (six-game heater) kept rolling; the Colts (eight straight losses), Packers (six straight losses) and Buccaneers (10 straight ATS defeats) kept failing; and the NFC South kept being, well, the NFC South (0-4 SU, 1-3 ATS).

What's in store for Week 2? Here's an NFL betting trends breakdown for five marquee matchups.

• With their come-from-behind 39-22 victory against Green Bay as a two-point favorite in Week 1, the Vikings have now won six straight games dating to Week 14 of last season (5-0-1 ATS).

During this stretch, the defense has yielded an average of 12.3 points per contest, with only the Packers (last week) and Cowboys (34-26 loss in Week 15 last year) topping 13 points.

• In walloping Carolina 59-37 as a 3-point favorite in Week 1, the Bears scored the fourth-most points in franchise history; tied for the second most in a season opener in NFL history; and started 1-0 for just the fourth time in the last 13 years.

Now Chicago will be looking to defy another NFL betting trend: Since 2014, the franchise has opened with back-to-back victories just once (in 2020, it started 3-0).

• Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' Week 1 stats were otherworldly: 21-for-29 for 269 passing yards; 65 rushing yards on 10 carries; and four total touchdowns (two passing, two rushing).

Williams has exactly two TD passes in eight straight games — including two playoff contests — and has thrown for multiple scores 10 times in his last 13 starts.

However, in two games against the Vikings last year, the former Heisman Trophy winner completed just 55% of his passes (37-for-67) for 403 yards and one TD.

• Minnesota is 9-3 versus the Bears since 2000 (7-4-1 ATS). This includes six consecutive victories at Soldier Field (4-1-1 ATS).

Five of the last six meetings overall were decided by six points or fewer. Final scores: 19-13, 12-10, 30-27 (overtime), 27-24, 19-17.

Cincinnati Bengals at Houston Texans (-2.5, 46.5)

• Cincinnati turned the first of four fumble recoveries into a 27-yard defensive touchdown and went on to top Tampa Bay 33-27 as a 3.5-point favorite in its opener.

It was just the third time in the last seven seasons that the Bengals posted a Week 1 victory. The franchise hasn't started 2-0 SU and ATS since 2018.

• In a game that featured 10 lead changes, Houston came out on the short end of a 36-31 contest against the Bills in Week 1, falling as a 1.5-point home underdog.

The defeat snapped a nine-game regular season winning streak and a seven-game home winning streak. The Texans haven't lost consecutive home contests since falling to Detroit (26-23) and Tennessee (32-27) in Weeks 10 and 12 of 2024.

However, since 2000, Houston is 1-5 SU in Week 2 — including last year's 20-19 loss to the Buccaneers as a 2.5-point home chalk.

• An interesting NFL betting trend related to Joe Burrow : In games he has started and finished since the 2023 season kicked off, the Bengals are 2-4 SU as a road underdog but 5-1 ATS.

That includes four consecutive spread covers: a pair of one-point losses at Baltimore and Kansas City in 2024, a 32-14 victory at Baltimore as a 7.5-point favorite and 39-34 loss at Buffalo as a 6.5-point underdog in consecutive weeks late last season.

• These teams have met six times since 2014, with the underdog going 5-1 SU and 6-0 ATS.

• These squads experienced near-opposite outcomes in Week 1: Jacksonville pummeled the Browns 34-10 as an 8.5-point home favorite for its ninth straight win and spread cover, while Denver got whacked 31-10 as a 2.5-point underdog at the Chiefs .

Despite Monday's night's uninspired effort in Kansas City, Denver is still 13-2 in its last 15 regular season outings. However, the other defeat came against Jacksonville late last year: In Week 16, the Jaguars cruised 34-20 as a 2.5-point road underdog, halting the Broncos' 11-game winning streak.

• During their nine-game hot streak, the Jaguars have averaged 36.7 PPG (tallying 34 points or more six times) and surrendered just 14 points per game (holding eight of nine opponents to less than 21 points).

Conversely, including two playoff games, Denver has produced 22 points or fewer in 12 of 20 contests since the start of last season. And its once-vaunted defense has permitted at least 26 points in five of the last nine outings.

• Since Sean Payton took over as head coach in 2023, the Broncos are now 2-8 SU and ATS in games prior to Week 4 — that includes 1-3 SU and 0-4 ATS marks both at home and as a favorite.

• A couple of NFL betting trends pertaining to the total in this game: The over is 8-3 in Jacksonville's last 11 regular season contests, with seven easily clearing 44 total points.

Also, going back to Week 3 of the 2024 season, the over has cashed in 12 of the Jaguars' 16 games outside of Jacksonville (including three played in London). All 12 hurdled 44 points.

Indianapolis Colts at Kansas City Chiefs (-6.5, 47.5)

• The Colts' defense got torched for 506 yards in a 41-23 season-opening loss to Baltimore as a three-point home underdog.

Since starting 8-2 SU and 6-3-1 ATS last season, Indianapolis has dropped eight consecutive games (3-5 ATS). One of those setbacks was a 23-20 overtime loss at Kansas City in Week 12, although the Colts covered as a 4.5-point underdog.

• The Chiefs closed out Week 1 with a 31-10 thumping of Denver as a 2.5-point home favorite on Monday night, with new running back (and reigning Super Bowl MVP) Kenneth Walker III producing more scrimmage yards by himself (191) than the entire Broncos offense (176).

It was Kansas City's first victory since edging Indy in November, as the franchise followed that with a season-ending six-game slide.

However, the Chiefs remain just 2-8 ATS in their last 10 games, with both spread covers coming at home against Denver.

• Since the start of last season, Kansas City is 5-10 ATS as a favorite, including an ongoing 0-8 ATS slump when laying three points or more.

Conversely, the Colts went 5-3 ATS as an underdog last season, and have cashed in three straight contests when catching more than four points.

Two other NFL betting trends of note: Since 2020, the Chiefs are 1-5 ATS in Week 2 (1-4 ATS as a favorite), while Indy is 4-2 ATS (3-0 ATS as an underdog).

• The under is 12-1 in the Chiefs' last 13 games, including 6-0 in the last six overall and 8-0 in the last eight in K.C.

Only two of the Chiefs' last 13 contests have hurdled 47 combined points. Both were on the road.

New York Giants at Los Angeles Rams (-7, 48.5)

• New York kicked off the John Harbaugh era in impressive fashion, dusting the rival Cowboys 28-20 as a three-point home underdog.

The Giants are 1-0 for just the third time in the last 15 years. Since 2010, they have opened 2-0 just twice (2016 and 2022). Only in 2022 did the G-Men win and cover their first two games.

• The Rams began the 2026 season as the overwhelming Super Bowl favorites, then traveled to Australia and fell flat in a 27-7 loss to NFC West rival San Francisco as 3.5-point chalk.

Despite that result, Los Angeles remains 21-9 SU and 20-10 ATS in its last 30 regular season games.

During this stretch, the Rams have suffered back-to-back defeats just once: In Weeks 16 and 17 last season, they fell 38-37 at Seattle in overtime (as a two-point underdog) and 27-24 at Atlanta (as a seven-point favorite).

• Including the playoffs, Los Angeles last season scored fewer than 22 points four times. The team's scoring output the following week: 33, 35, 34 and 27.

This week, the Rams face a defense that allowed an average of 28.3 points in its first 14 games in 2025. Since then, though, New York has held three opponents opponents — Minnesota, Las Vegas and Dallas twice — to 16, 10, 17 and 20 points.

• Going back to Week 6 of last season, the over is 11-2 in Giants games, although only seven of those contests cleared 48 points.

And while the Rams' Week 1 loss Down Under stayed well under the total, the over is still 8-2 in their last 10 games (playoffs included). All eight flew past 50 combined points.

articles.title: Tee Higgins says Joe Burrow 'looked good' in practice ahead of Week 2
articles.summary: Joe Burrow's teammates give latest update on their quarterback following practice on Sept. 17.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow sent the NFL news cycle into a frenzy on Sept. 17 when he was a limited participant in practice.

The number of serious injuries he's endured early in his career is the reason why ears will always perk up when there's any talk of a potential health issue.

He's missed 25 games in his professional career due to significant injuries that required surgery on his knee, toe and wrist. Injuries are very much part of Burrow's NFL story so far.

Burrow told reporters in Cincinnati that he's dealing with back tightness but expects to play against the Houston Texans on Sept. 20 at Reliant Stadium.

After a day that consisted mostly of "mental reps" during practice on Sept. 16, Burrow's workload was increased one day later. Burrow took part in team stretch and was seen throwing passes as he typically does during the portion of practice that's open to the media on Sept. 17. He did neither of those things on Sept. 16 and was listed as a limited participant in practice on the team's official report.

Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins said Burrow did a lot more in practice Thursday. Higgins said Burrow "looked good" and said the team is looking to stack days of strong preparation ahead of the Week 2 matchup against the Texans (0-1).

Typically for the Bengals, the second practice of the week is when most action occurs. It's why Burrow being able to participate at a higher level on Sept. 17 is noteworthy. Prior to practice, Burrow was seen doing his normal quarterback-center exchange work with Ted Karras .

Following practice, Karras spoke of how his quarterback looked during the two-hour session.

"Great," Karras said. "We had a great Thursday practice. We're (back to) normal programming. We need to go win in Houston at noon; it's a big week."

For the Bengals to beat the Texans on the road, Burrow and the rest of Cincinnati's offense will need to play well. Houston owned the NFL's best defense in 2025 (17.4 points per game), and most of the unit returned for the 2026 season.

The Bills showed Houston's defense is capable of giving up 30-plus points, though. Buffalo beat Houston 36-31 in Week 1. The Bengals are hoping to start the season 2-0 for a second consecutive year under head coach Zac Taylor.

"It would me a lot, that's what we're looking forward to doing," Higgins said.

articles.title: NFL Week 2 Fantasy Football injury report: Brock Bowers and more
articles.summary: There are many fantasy decisions to be made for Week 2. Included in that mix is the right approach to the waiver wire. But there are also injury concerns,...
articles.body:
There are many fantasy decisions to be made for Week 2 . Included in that mix is the right approach to the waiver wire . But there are also injury concerns, and here is the NFL fantasy football injury report, including Brock Bowers , Kyler Murray , and more.

It has already been a very disappointing start to the season for managers of Bowers and Murray. Bowers was expected to be the best fantasy tight end in the NFL. Murray's draft status suggested he could be a later-round difference-maker. But they combined for only a handful of snaps in Week 1.

Let's take a look at this week's rundown.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

What exactly do the Vikings have in Murray? He went 3 of 5 for 18 yards and a terrible interception before getting hurt. The thing with concussions is that players can't be rushed back.

Murray got through a limited practice on Wednesday, according to NBC Sports.

"We'll see how he responds and continue to rely on the medical folks in that regard," Vikings head coach Kevin O'Connell said. "The good thing is the amount of reps he got from obviously competing and then being named the starter. He's got a lot of reps logged away. But, yeah, really we're taking it kind of period-by-period as far as the plan we have. But we want to be monitoring how he's doing from a standpoint of that limited participation.

"It's a little bit more of a vague thing at the quarterback position, just because they're in red jerseys anyway all the way up until game time. So we'll kind of just deal with it as it comes to us."

Darnold won't play in Week 2, but the belief remains that this won't be a long-term absence. Still, it could linger, according to ESPN.

"According to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, multiple sources are bracing for Darnold to miss roughly four weeks from the time of his injury but are hoping he can come back sooner," Brady Henderson wrote. "One source told Fowler that Darnold returning for the 49ers game in Week 5 feels like a possibility. Another source estimated that he'll be sidelined for three to four weeks and added that the quarterback is moving around much better in recent days."

There's a defiant take by Burrow about whether he would miss the game against the Texans just for precautionary reasons, according to ESPN.

"That's ridiculous," Burrow said. "I think every game is important. I'll do what it takes to be out there. If I'm not having surgery, I'll be out there."

Fantasy managers of Burrow have to like that attitude. Things seem to be in a good place for him to play.

Even if he's ready to go, it doesn't sound like the Falcons have committed to putting him back on the field, according to Fox News.

"Of course, ideal world, I think everybody, every team, you'd love to know who's playing at every position," Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said. "That's a no-brainer. I get that part. But we're going to be flexible and make sure that we're giving all of our guys the ability to go play and play well."

And Tagovailoa's fate may have been sealed when he didn't practice Thursday while Michael Penix Jr. and Cooper Rush were full participants.

It's a process, but Penix believes he's working toward a return, according to ajc.com.

"I'm close," Penix said. "I know I've been saying that, but there's just a couple technical things that I want to hit. Some goals that I have that I want to achieve before I do stuff out on that field. But I do feel really good, and we're taking strides each and every day."

His return to full practice Thursday puts him trending in the right direction.

RB TreVeyon Henderson , Patriots (ankle)

Things are looking up for Henderson to make his 2026 debut, according to a post on X by Mike Reiss.

"RB TreVeyon Henderson: 'I'm ready to go.' "

This is tremendous good news for Henderson and the Patriots. Receiver A.J. Brown is out with an injury, which means Henderson's explosiveness is more critical to have on the field. Plus, he can serve as a threat in the passing game. Getting him back doesn't solve the Brown situation, but it helps.

Getting on the field looks like a good possibility for Kamara this week. He practiced fully on Wednesday, according to ESPN.

"I think it was just a matter of time on task, getting a full week's work," Saints head coach Kellen Moore said. "I (thought) he did an amazing job to put himself in a position last week to practice really well. And so he's in a great place."

The Saints need Kamara, according to quarterback Tyler Shough .

"He's a difference-maker at every position, to be honest," Shough said. "His physicality, his speed, his one-cut ability, his presence, just in the huddle, just from just all that stuff. He's got the experience, and then they have to respect all that stuff.

Mason had surgery and won't play again until at least mid-October. He was placed on injured reserve. Fortunately, the Vikings have a capable runner in Aaron Jones , who can take on an expanded role — even at the age of 31. Rookie Demond Claiborne could also get his first NFL touches.

This isn't a great situation as Collins appeared on the injury report Wednesday. He had a limited appearance, which provides some hope. But this situation bears watching.

Fortunately, it doesn't appear to be a serious injury , according to a post on X by Adam Schefter.

"Texans WR Nico Collins injured his hamstring at Wednesday's practice, met with doctors after, and they 'don't believe it's serious,' per source. Yet Collins' status for Sunday's game vs. the Bengals is in jeopardy."

Flowers didn't make it to the practice field on Wednesday or Thursday. There is growing concern he could miss Week 2. And that may be best , according to The Athletic.

"Realistically, a week of inactivity is probably the best thing for Flowers," Andy Behrens wrote. "Hamstring injuries are notoriously stubborn."

It doesn't help the Flowers situation that Lane is expected to miss multiple weeks because of a fractured wrist in the season opener. Still, the team hopes to have him back soon, according to ESPN.

"[Lane] definitely has a really good chance coming back here pretty quick," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said. "I know he'll be chomping at the bit to get back."

With the two Ravens injuries, Rashod Bateman is a good fantasy play this week.

Missing practice on Wednesday, McConkey faces a battle to get on the field in Week 2. Quarterback Justin Herbert wants him back soon, according to ESPN.

"Ladd's a really good football player," quarterback Justin Herbert said. "We're really glad to have him, and he made a ton of plays today, so I'm hoping he feels better."

Don't sleep on Tre' Harris for fantasy if McConkey can't go.

WR Brian Thomas Jr. , Jaguars (shoulder)

Good news for the Jaguars, as it looks like Thomas will be able to go against the Broncos . And he still has a chance to be a fantasy bounce-back this season.

Getting in a full practice Wednesday, Pierce should be able to avoid an injury designation for this weekend.

But whether he should play in fantasy against the Chiefs is questionable, according to Sports Illustrated.

"I am still unsure whether I want to trust Pierce this week," Thomas Carelli wrote. "My projections list Pierce at a 16% yard share in Week 2 and the WR59. The real knot in the start-sit debate lies with his opponent, the Kansas City Chiefs . In Week 1, the Chiefs were rated the 4th-best in coverage based on EPA/Pass (-0.449).

Don't look for Cooper to get back this week. But he likely avoided a long-term absence, according to NFL.com.

"An MRI revealed positive news, per NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is week to week," the NFL.com staff wrote. "With the hope that he returns within the next four weeks, Rapoport reported."

A full participant Wednesday and Thursday, McMillan should be good to go for Sunday. That's good news for quarterback Baker Mayfield , according to buccaneers.com.

"He brings a different dynamic, being able to separate in coverage, a different level of juice," Mayfield said. "And also somebody that when he makes plays you can feel the energy on the sideline. You can feel it from him. And he elevates the standard."

Pittman missed the open portion of Thursday's practice. That's not a good sign this late in the week.

Missing practice Wednesday is more disappointing news for Bowers. He played only 12 games last season, and seems headed for a short season again this year.

Of course, if he makes it back this week, he could change that narrative. And there's hope , according to NBC Sports.

"Head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters in his Wednesday press conference that Bowers (knee) is not yet ready to practice," Myles Simmons wrote. "But Kubiak said he's hopeful that Bowers will be able to return this week."

It wasn't a great debut with his new team. And now he's injured. The Commanders are holding out hope that Okonkwo will be able to play against the Cowboys.

articles.title: Las Vegas NFL QB admits to wild 9-patty In-N-Out order
articles.summary: "I have an In-N-Out problem."
articles.body:
There's just something about In-N-Out . For decades, the California-founded burger chain has drawn national attention for its quality, simplicity and slow-scale approach. And while in recent years billionaire owner Lynsi Snyder has pushed the company's boundaries ever eastward , the Southern California company still considers Las Vegas to be a second home of sorts - even adding a giant new flagship store right on the Las Vegas Strip this summer.

And as it turns out, one of the brand's most high-profile megafans also happens to reside in Las Vegas: Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins.

"I have an In-N-Out problem," the NFL veteran said cheerfully during a press conference this week before the team's Sunday game against the Los Angeles Chargers.

"It wasn't a big deal when I lived in the Central or Eastern time zone," he added, "but on the West Coast time zone, when I signed with the Raiders, I knew this was gonna be an issue." Cousins has previously played for the Minnesota Vikings, Atlanta Falcons and Washington Commanders.

Cousins was then asked about his specific order, and that's where things got interesting.

"I actually have a go-to, but it's one I'm not very proud of," he said with a smirk. "If I'm really hungry - and I did this in August on an off day - I had three 3x3s." In In-N-Out lingo, a 3x3 means three beef patties and three cheese slices on a single burger. But Cousins wasn't done. "I don't get onions, but then I also get fries. Don't usually do a shake. That's probably the one discipline I try to have."

Long ago, Cousins would have been able to simply order a 9x9 burger - nine patties and nine cheese slices in a single, giant bun - but those days are long gone. In-N-Out no longer allows burger size modifications above a 4x4, after a Bay Area tech worker and his friends famously ordered and received a 100x100 burger on Halloween night in 2004. (Ironically, the location that made the monstrosity was also located in Las Vegas.)

Within his answer, Cousins also outlined his unusually focused approach to ordering - or, more specifically, to trying to beat In-N-Out's notoriously long and egalitarian lines . "I'm not a very patient person, so waiting in the lines can be tough," he says (great self-scouting). "So I tend to park and go in. In my mind, I tell myself that's faster. I don't know if it actually is or not." For what it's worth, internet sleuths are divided on whether drive-thru or ordering inside makes for the shorter wait time.

Cousins added that he's still putting in reps to test his ordering hypothesis. "I try to be strategic when I go, as far as wait times," he said. "I haven't quite figured out that hack. Maybe it's early, 10:30 a.m. - 11 a.m. when they first open."

The Raiders play the San Francisco 49ers on Nov. 8 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara. Kirk, if you're reading this: The closest In-N-Out location to the stadium is just over 2 miles away on Mission College Boulevard.

articles.title: Michael Penix Jr. injury update as Falcons QB practices ahead of Week 2
articles.summary: Michael Penix Jr. was a full participant at Thursday's practice. Will that allow him to suit up for the Falcons in Week 2?
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons were without their top two quarterbacks, Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa , for their Week 1 loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers .

Will either quarterback be available for the Falcons in Week 2? At least one is taking positive steps as Atlanta prepares to host the Carolina Panthers for its home opener, as Penix was once again a full participant at the Falcons' practice on Thursday, Sept. 17.

Penix has been a full participant at each of the Falcons' five official practice sessions to date in 2026 as he seeks to return from a torn ACL he suffered against the Panthers in Week 11 of the 2025 season.

That may be an encouraging sign for Penix, but does it mean his return to the field will be imminent? Or will the Falcons once again start third-stringer Cooper Rush to give the 2024 first-round pick more time to work back to full strength?

Here's what to know about Penix's status ahead of the Falcons' Week 2 game against the Panthers.

Notable injuries throughout the 2026 NFL season

Penix officially logged full participation at Falcons practice on Thursday, according to their official injury report .

While that was similar to what Penix did in Week 1, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski revealed in a Thursday interview with 92.9 The Game that there was a "progression" in how they were treating the 26-year-old quarterback entering Week 2.

"We ruled Mike out early last week, "Stefanski explained. "We didn't rule Mike out this week."

Still, Stefanski wouldn't commit to Penix getting the nod as the Week 2 starter, preaching patience about the 2024 first-round pick's continued recovery from his knee injury.

"We're continuing to practice and progress and do different things, but I wouldn't read much into anything other that we'll be really smart about this," Stefanski said. "Mike and I talk every day. I talk to the medical staff every day. We all are on the same page and we'll continue to be on the same page."

As mentioned, Stefanski wasn't yet ready to name a starting quarterback for Week 2. He did, however, indicate he would "know more" about his decision after Thursday's session.

"Whether or not we make a decision today, I can't say that for sure," Stefanski told 92.9 The Game. "But I'll know more after today."

The expectation is that Stefanski will choose between Penix and Rush, the team's veteran third-string quarterback. Tagovailoa was unable to practice on Thursday because of his back injury, suggesting he may not yet be ready to return to the field.

Below is a look at the Falcons' quarterback depth chart as they continue to deal with injuries among their top players at the position.

Tagovailoa and Penix competed for the Falcons' starting job during training camp, with the former winning by default after Penix couldn't play in the preseason. But now, because of Tagovailoa's injury, Penix will likely be given a chance to stake his claim to the starting job, whether he returns in Week 2 or later.

Rush started for the Falcons in Week 1 against the Steelers. The 32-year-old struggled, completing 12 of 22 passes for 143 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while being sacked four times in Atlanta's 20-13 loss to Pittsburgh.

Strand is an undrafted rookie from Minnesota State – Moorhead who performed well in the preseason but has never played a regular-season snap.
